2	// Grokfast — vendor-neutral algorithm header.
3	//
4	// Reference: Lee et al. 2024, "Grokfast: Accelerated Grokking by
5	// Amplifying Slow Gradients" (https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.20233),
6	// EMA-amplified gradient form.
7	//
8	// Simplest grokking-aware AdamW: EMA filter + amplification, then standard
9	// Adam. Two operational modes:
10	//
11	//   (A) ema-only:   ema = alpha * ema + (1-alpha) * g;
12	//                   grad_out = g + lamb * ema       (consumed by downstream Adam)
13	//
14	//   (B) fused:      same EMA update, then immediately run Adam on g_amp.
15	//
16	// Calling convention: bc1, bc2 are passed un-inverted —
17	//   bc1 = 1 - beta1^t,  bc2 = 1 - beta2^t.

20	#include "csrc/common/utils.cuh"

22	namespace sg { namespace algorithms {
23	
24	// EMA-only path: update EMA and write amplified gradient back into grad_out.
25	template <typename GradT>
26	__device__ __forceinline__ void grokfast_ema_step(
27	    float* __restrict__ ema,
28	    GradT* __restrict__ grad_out,
29	    const GradT* __restrict__ grad_in,
30	    const float alpha,
31	    const float lamb,
32	    const int64_t idx
33	) {
34	    const float g = static_cast<float>(grad_in[idx]);
35	    const float e = alpha * ema[idx] + (1.0f - alpha) * g;
36	    ema[idx] = e;
37	    grad_out[idx] = static_cast<GradT>(g + lamb * e);
38	}
39	
40	// Fully fused: EMA + amplification + AdamW in a single per-element step.
41	// Keeps the amplified gradient in registers from compute through Adam.
42	template <typename ParamT, typename GradT>
43	__device__ __forceinline__ void grokfast_fused_step(
44	    ParamT* __restrict__ param,
45	    float* __restrict__ exp_avg,
46	    float* __restrict__ exp_avg_sq,
47	    float* __restrict__ ema,
48	    const GradT* __restrict__ grad,
49	    const float grokfast_alpha,
50	    const float grokfast_lamb,
51	    const float lr,
52	    const float beta1,
53	    const float beta2,
54	    const float eps,
55	    const float wd,
56	    const float bc1,
57	    const float bc2,
58	    const int64_t idx
59	) {
60	    const float g = static_cast<float>(grad[idx]);
61	    const float p = static_cast<float>(param[idx]);
62	
63	    const float e_new = grokfast_alpha * ema[idx] + (1.0f - grokfast_alpha) * g;
64	    ema[idx] = e_new;
65	    const float g_amp = g + grokfast_lamb * e_new;
66	
67	    const float m = beta1 * exp_avg[idx]    + (1.0f - beta1) * g_amp;
68	    const float v = beta2 * exp_avg_sq[idx] + (1.0f - beta2) * g_amp * g_amp;
69	    exp_avg[idx]    = m;
70	    exp_avg_sq[idx] = v;
71	
72	    // bc1, bc2 un-inverted (= 1 - beta^t): divide for bias correction.
73	    const float update = (m / sg_safe_bc(bc1)) / (sqrtf(v / sg_safe_bc(bc2)) + eps);
74	    param[idx] = static_cast<ParamT>(p - lr * (update + wd * p));
75	}

15	//   v_hat = v_t / (1 - beta2^t)

67	// g_eff. This is the SINGLE source of the moment-update + decoupled-WD apply
68	// math, factored out of grokadamw_step so storage-variant kernels (e.g. the
69	// quantized Config-3 path, which dequantizes/requantizes the state) can reuse
70	// the exact same float ops without re-inlining them. Produces m_out, v_out
71	// (the new moments) and p_out (the new parameter value) by reference; the
72	// caller is responsible for writing them back (FP32 or quantized).
73	//
74	// Bit-identical to the tail of grokadamw_step:
75	//   m = beta1 * m_prev + (1 - beta1) * g_eff;
76	//   v = beta2 * v_prev + (1 - beta2) * g_eff * g_eff;
77	//   update = (m / bc1) / (sqrtf(v / bc2) + eps);
78	//   p_out  = p - lr * (update + wd * p);
79	__device__ __forceinline__ void grokadamw_adam_tail(
80	    const float g_eff,
81	    const float p,
82	    const float m_prev,
83	    const float v_prev,
84	    const float lr,
85	    const float beta1,
86	    const float beta2,
87	    const float eps,
88	    const float wd,
89	    const float bc1,
90	    const float bc2,
91	    float& m_out,
92	    float& v_out,
93	    float& p_out
94	) {
95	    const float m = beta1 * m_prev + (1.0f - beta1) * g_eff;
96	    const float v = beta2 * v_prev + (1.0f - beta2) * g_eff * g_eff;
97	    const float update = (m / sg_safe_bc(bc1)) / (sqrtf(v / sg_safe_bc(bc2)) + eps);
98	    m_out = m;
99	    v_out = v;
100	    p_out = p - lr * (update + wd * p);
101	}
102	
103	}} // namespace sg::algorithms

1	#pragma once
2	// LookSAM — vendor-neutral algorithm header.
3	//
4	// Reference: Liu et al. 2022, "Towards Efficient and Scalable Sharpness-
5	// Aware Minimization" (https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.02714), Algorithm 1
6	// (periodic-perturbation variant — SAM gradient is recomputed every k
7	// steps, then reused as a cached direction for intervening steps).
8	//
9	// AdamW with periodic Sharpness-Aware Minimization (every k steps).
10	//
11	// Four operations:
12	//   (1) perturb:           p_pert = p + rho * (g / ||g||)
13	//   (2) restore:           p = p_pert - rho * (g / ||g||)
14	//   (3) direction adjust:  on SAM step,    sam_dir = g_sam - g
15	//                          on normal step, g_adj   = (1-alpha)*g + alpha*sam_dir
16	//   (4) standard AdamW update with g_adj.
17	//
18	// Calling convention: bc1, bc2 are passed un-inverted —
19	//   bc1 = 1 - beta1^t,  bc2 = 1 - beta2^t.
20	
21	#include "csrc/common/types.h"
22	#include "csrc/common/utils.cuh"
23	
24	namespace sg { namespace algorithms {
25	
26	// Step (1) — perturb in gradient direction by rho / ||g||.
27	template <typename ParamT, typename GradT>
28	__device__ __forceinline__ void looksam_perturb_step(
29	    ParamT* __restrict__ param,
30	    ParamT* __restrict__ backup,
31	    const GradT* __restrict__ grad,
32	    const float scale,        // rho / (||g|| + eps), precomputed
33	    const int64_t idx
34	) {
35	    const ParamT p = param[idx];
36	    backup[idx] = p;
37	    param[idx] = static_cast<ParamT>(static_cast<float>(p) + scale * static_cast<float>(grad[idx]));
38	}
39	
40	// Step (2) — restore parameters from backup.
41	template <typename ParamT>
42	__device__ __forceinline__ void looksam_restore_step(
43	    ParamT* __restrict__ param,
44	    const ParamT* __restrict__ backup,
45	    const int64_t idx
46	) {
47	    param[idx] = backup[idx];
48	}
49	
50	// Step (3) on SAM step: cache the gradient difference.
51	template <typename GradT>
52	__device__ __forceinline__ void looksam_set_direction(
53	    float* __restrict__ sam_dir,
54	    const GradT* __restrict__ grad_sam,
55	    const GradT* __restrict__ grad_orig,
56	    const int64_t idx
57	) {
58	    sam_dir[idx] = static_cast<float>(grad_sam[idx]) - static_cast<float>(grad_orig[idx]);
59	}
60	
61	// Step (3) on normal step + Step (4): blend cached SAM direction and run Adam.
62	template <typename ParamT, typename GradT>
63	__device__ __forceinline__ void looksam_apply_step(
64	    ParamT* __restrict__ param,
65	    float* __restrict__ exp_avg,
66	    float* __restrict__ exp_avg_sq,
67	    const float* __restrict__ sam_dir,
68	    const GradT* __restrict__ grad,
69	    const float alpha,         // SAM blend strength
70	    const float lr,
71	    const float beta1,
72	    const float beta2,
73	    const float eps,
74	    const float wd,
75	    const float bc1,
76	    const float bc2,
77	    const int64_t idx
78	) {
79	    const float g = static_cast<float>(grad[idx]);
80	    const float p = static_cast<float>(param[idx]);
81	    const float g_adj = (1.0f - alpha) * g + alpha * sam_dir[idx];
82	
83	    const float m = beta1 * exp_avg[idx]    + (1.0f - beta1) * g_adj;
84	    const float v = beta2 * exp_avg_sq[idx] + (1.0f - beta2) * g_adj * g_adj;
85	    exp_avg[idx]    = m;
86	    exp_avg_sq[idx] = v;
87	
88	    // bc1, bc2 un-inverted (= 1 - beta^t): divide for bias correction.
89	    const float update = (m / sg_safe_bc(bc1)) / (sqrtf(v / sg_safe_bc(bc2)) + eps);
90	    param[idx] = static_cast<ParamT>(p - lr * (update + wd * p));
91	}
92	
93	}} // namespace sg::algorithms

1	#pragma once
2	// Muon — vendor-neutral algorithm header.
3	//
4	// Dual-strategy optimizer:
5	//   2D parameters: Newton-Schulz orthogonalized momentum
6	//   1D parameters: standard AdamW
7	//
8	// Per-element pieces (the heavy lifting — matrix multiplications for NS —
9	// lives in primitives.cuh / mma.cuh per backend):
10	//
11	//   momentum_normalize:  buf = momentum * buf + grad;   (plain SGD-momentum —
12	//                        no (1 - momentum) factor; matches the implementation
13	//                        below and bindings.cpp::muon_fused_step)
14	//                        X    = buf / ||buf||_F     (Frobenius-normalized)
15	//   ns_combine:          Y = a*X + b*A_X + c*AA_X    (polynomial combine)
16	//   muon_update:         param = param * decay + neg_lr_scale * orth
17	
18	#include "csrc/common/types.h"
19	#include "csrc/common/utils.cuh"
20	#include "csrc/algorithms/adamw.h"
21	
22	namespace sg { namespace algorithms {
23	
24	// Momentum normalize: buf = momentum * buf + grad, then X = buf * inv_norm.
25	//
26	// Reference: Jordan et al. 2024, "Muon: An optimizer for the orthogonal
27	// manifold" (https://kellerjordan.github.io/posts/muon/). The momentum
28	// update is plain SGD-momentum (no (1-momentum) factor on the gradient),
29	// matching the active multi-tensor path in
30	// csrc/bindings/bindings.cpp::muon_fused_step (bufs[i].mul_(momentum).add_(grads[i])).
31	// Newton-Schulz iteration (5 steps by default) follows the standard
32	// (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) polynomial recurrence from the same source.
33	template <typename GradT>
34	__device__ __forceinline__ void muon_momentum_normalize_step(
35	    float* __restrict__ buf,
36	    float* __restrict__ X,
37	    const GradT* __restrict__ grad,
38	    const float momentum,
39	    const float inv_norm,
40	    const int64_t idx
41	) {
42	    const float g = static_cast<float>(grad[idx]);
43	    const float b = momentum * buf[idx] + g;
44	    buf[idx] = b;
45	    X[idx] = b * inv_norm;
46	}
47	
48	// Polynomial combine: Y = a*X + b*AX + c*AAX  (Newton-Schulz iteration body).
49	__device__ __forceinline__ void muon_ns_combine_step(
50	    float* __restrict__ Y,
51	    const float* __restrict__ X,
52	    const float* __restrict__ AX,
53	    const float* __restrict__ AAX,
54	    const float a,
55	    const float b,
56	    const float c,
57	    const int64_t idx
58	) {
59	    Y[idx] = a * X[idx] + b * AX[idx] + c * AAX[idx];
60	}
61	
62	// Final parameter update with trust-ratio scaling.
63	template <typename ParamT>
64	__device__ __forceinline__ void muon_update_step(
65	    ParamT* __restrict__ param,
66	    const float* __restrict__ orth,
67	    const float neg_lr_scale,
68	    const float decay_factor,
69	    const int64_t idx
70	) {
71	    const float p = static_cast<float>(param[idx]);
72	    param[idx] = static_cast<ParamT>(p * decay_factor + neg_lr_scale * orth[idx]);
73	}
74	
75	// 1D parameters use AdamW directly.
76	using sg::algorithms::adamw_step;
77	
78	}} // namespace sg::algorithms

1	#pragma once
2	// Prodigy — vendor-neutral algorithm header.
3	//
4	// Reference: Mishchenko & Defazio 2023, "Prodigy: An Expeditiously
5	// Adaptive Parameter-Free Learner" (https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.06101),
6	// Algorithm 1 (D-Adaptation-style trajectory estimator + AdamW apply).
7	//
8	// Self-tuning Adam. Estimates its own learning rate d from the cumulative
9	// parameter trajectory: d_new = max(d_prev, r / s), where r and s are
10	// global reductions across all parameters (s is the L1 norm ||·||_1):
11	//   r += grad * (param_init - param) * d_prev * d_prev   (degree-2 -> scale-free)
12	//   s += d_prev * d_prev * |grad|
13	//
14	// Three operations:
15	//   (1) reduce: compute partial r, s sums (block-level)
16	//   (2) update: combine partials, update d on a single device thread
17	//   (3) apply:  AdamW step using d (loaded from device memory)
18	//
19	// Calling convention: bc1, bc2 are passed un-inverted —
20	//   bc1 = 1 - beta1^t,  bc2 = 1 - beta2^t.
21	
22	#include "csrc/common/types.h"
23	#include "csrc/common/utils.cuh"
24	
25	namespace sg { namespace algorithms {
26	
27	// Per-element contribution to r and s partial sums.
28	template <typename ParamT, typename GradT>
29	__device__ __forceinline__ void prodigy_partials_step(
30	    const ParamT* __restrict__ param,
31	    const ParamT* __restrict__ param_init,
32	    const GradT* __restrict__ grad,
33	    const float d_prev,
34	    const int64_t idx,
35	    float& r_local,
36	    float& s_local
37	) {
38	    const float p  = static_cast<float>(param[idx]);
39	    const float pi = static_cast<float>(param_init[idx]);
40	    const float g  = static_cast<float>(grad[idx]);
41	
42	    // Numerator and denominator must carry the SAME power of d so the estimate
43	    // d_hat = r/s is scale-free (degree 0 in d). The denominator carries d²
44	    // (below), so the numerator carries d² too. A degree-1 numerator (a single
45	    // d_prev) made d_hat ∝ 1/d, which at the d0 = 1e-6 init blew d up by ~1e6×
46	    // in a single step (catapult) and destroyed training — the fused kernel
47	    // matched the canonical paper formula's intent only once both sides are d².
48	    r_local += g * (pi - p) * d_prev * d_prev;
49	    // Prodigy d-estimate denominator is the L1 norm ||s||_1 = Σ_j |d²·g_j|
50	    // (arxiv 2306.06101), so accumulate |g| per coordinate. (Previously this
51	    // summed signed g and took |Σ| at reduce time — abs-of-sum ≠ L1 norm.)
52	    s_local += d_prev * d_prev * fabsf(g);
53	}
54	
55	// d update — runs on a single thread once r_sum and s_sum are reduced.
56	__device__ __forceinline__ float prodigy_update_d(
57	    const float d_prev,
58	    const float r_sum,
59	    const float s_sum
60	) {
61	    const float denom = fabsf(s_sum);
62	    if (denom < 1e-12f) return d_prev;
63	    const float candidate = r_sum / denom;
64	    return fmaxf(d_prev, candidate);
65	}
66	
67	// Apply: AdamW with d as the effective learning rate scale.
68	template <typename ParamT, typename GradT>
69	__device__ __forceinline__ void prodigy_apply_step(
70	    ParamT* __restrict__ param,
71	    float* __restrict__ exp_avg,
72	    float* __restrict__ exp_avg_sq,
73	    float* __restrict__ s_track,     // trajectory accumulator
74	    const GradT* __restrict__ grad,
75	    const float d,                   // adaptive learning rate
76	    const float beta1,
77	    const float beta2,
78	    const float eps,
79	    const float wd,
80	    const float bc1,
81	    const float bc2,
82	    const int64_t idx
83	) {
84	    const float g = static_cast<float>(grad[idx]);
85	    const float p = static_cast<float>(param[idx]);
86	
87	    const float g_scaled = d * g;
88	    const float m = beta1 * exp_avg[idx]    + (1.0f - beta1) * g_scaled;
89	    const float v = beta2 * exp_avg_sq[idx] + (1.0f - beta2) * g_scaled * g_scaled;
90	    exp_avg[idx]    = m;
91	    exp_avg_sq[idx] = v;
92	    s_track[idx]   += d * g;
93	
94	    // bc1, bc2 un-inverted (= 1 - beta^t): divide for bias correction.
95	    const float update = (m / sg_safe_bc(bc1)) / (sqrtf(v / sg_safe_bc(bc2)) + eps);
96	    param[idx] = static_cast<ParamT>(p - d * (update + wd * p));
97	}
98	
99	}} // namespace sg::algorithms

2	// NeuralGrok — vendor-neutral algorithm header.
3	//
4	// Reference: Wang et al. 2024, "NeuralGrok: Accelerating Grokking via
5	// Learned Gradient Amplification" — Adam with a learned per-element
6	// amplifier (psi-net).
7	//
8	// The amplifier is a 2-layer MLP that takes |grad| as input and outputs
9	// a multiplicative scale.
10	//
11	// Two-stage compute:
12	//   (1) psi_net forward:  s = mlp(|g|)  (per-element scaling factor)
13	//   (2) apply:            g_amp = (s * alpha + beta) * g
14	//                         AdamW step on g_amp
15	//
16	// Calling convention: bc1, bc2 are passed un-inverted —
17	//   bc1 = 1 - beta1^t,  bc2 = 1 - beta2^t.
18	//
19	// The MLP weights live in constant memory on CUDA / LDS on HIP. The math
20	// here is the per-element body; the matmul is handled by the backend.
21	
22	#include "csrc/common/types.h"
23	#include "csrc/common/utils.cuh"
24	
25	namespace sg { namespace algorithms {
26	
27	// 2-layer MLP forward for a single element, with weights passed inline.
28	// W1: [H], b1: [H], W2: [H], b2: scalar.
29	// Activation: ReLU on hidden layer.
30	template <int H>
31	__device__ __forceinline__ float neuralgrok_psi_forward(
32	    const float abs_grad,
33	    const float* __restrict__ W1,
34	    const float* __restrict__ b1,
35	    const float* __restrict__ W2,
36	    const float b2
37	) {
38	    float h_acc = 0.0f;
39	    #pragma unroll
40	    for (int j = 0; j < H; j++) {
41	        float h = W1[j] * abs_grad + b1[j];
42	        h = (h > 0.0f) ? h : 0.0f;       // ReLU
43	        h_acc += W2[j] * h;
44	    }
45	    return h_acc + b2;
46	}
47	
48	// Apply: g_amp = (s * alpha + beta) * g, then run AdamW on g_amp.
49	template <typename ParamT, typename GradT>
50	__device__ __forceinline__ void neuralgrok_apply_step(
51	    ParamT* __restrict__ param,
52	    float* __restrict__ exp_avg,
53	    float* __restrict__ exp_avg_sq,
54	    const GradT* __restrict__ grad,
55	    const float psi_scale,        // output of psi_net forward
56	    const float alpha,
57	    const float beta,
58	    const float lr,
59	    const float beta1,
60	    const float beta2,
61	    const float eps,
62	    const float wd,
63	    const float bc1,
64	    const float bc2,
65	    const int64_t idx,
66	    const float clip_coef = 1.0f   // eager GLOBAL grad-norm clip coef (1.0 = inert); applied before psi+amp
67	) {
68	    const float g = static_cast<float>(grad[idx]) * clip_coef;
69	    const float p = static_cast<float>(param[idx]);
70	
71	    const float g_amp = (psi_scale * alpha + beta) * g;
72	
73	    const float m = beta1 * exp_avg[idx]    + (1.0f - beta1) * g_amp;
74	    const float v = beta2 * exp_avg_sq[idx] + (1.0f - beta2) * g_amp * g_amp;
75	    exp_avg[idx]    = m;
76	    exp_avg_sq[idx] = v;
77	
78	    // bc1, bc2 un-inverted (= 1 - beta^t): divide for bias correction.
79	    const float update = (m / sg_safe_bc(bc1)) / (sqrtf(v / sg_safe_bc(bc2)) + eps);
80	    param[idx] = static_cast<ParamT>(p - lr * (update + wd * p));
81	}
82	
83	// Canonical bias-corrected Adam tail on a caller-supplied effective gradient
84	// g_eff. SINGLE source of the moment-update + decoupled-WD apply math, factored
85	// out of neuralgrok_apply_step so the "Adam-only on a pre-amplified gradient"
86	// kernel can reuse the exact same float ops without re-inlining them. Writes
87	// the new moments into exp_avg[idx]/exp_avg_sq[idx] and the new parameter into
88	// param[idx].
89	//
90	// Bit-identical to the tail of neuralgrok_apply_step:
91	//   m = beta1 * exp_avg[idx]    + (1 - beta1) * g_eff;
92	//   v = beta2 * exp_avg_sq[idx] + (1 - beta2) * g_eff * g_eff;
93	//   update = (m / bc1) / (sqrtf(v / bc2) + eps);
94	//   param[idx] = p - lr * (update + wd * p);
95	template <typename ParamT>
96	__device__ __forceinline__ void neuralgrok_adam_tail(
97	    ParamT* __restrict__ param,
98	    float* __restrict__ exp_avg,
99	    float* __restrict__ exp_avg_sq,
100	    const float g_eff,
101	    const float lr,
102	    const float beta1,
103	    const float beta2,
104	    const float eps,
105	    const float wd,
106	    const float bc1,
107	    const float bc2,
108	    const int64_t idx
109	) {
110	    const float p = static_cast<float>(param[idx]);
111	    const float m = beta1 * exp_avg[idx]    + (1.0f - beta1) * g_eff;
112	    const float v = beta2 * exp_avg_sq[idx] + (1.0f - beta2) * g_eff * g_eff;
113	    exp_avg[idx]    = m;
114	    exp_avg_sq[idx] = v;
115	    const float update = (m / sg_safe_bc(bc1)) / (sqrtf(v / sg_safe_bc(bc2)) + eps);

1	#pragma once
2	// SuperGrok v1.1 — vendor-neutral algorithm header.
3	//
4	// Reference: internal algorithm. The Python source of truth is
5	// `grokking_optimizers/optimizers/supergrok11.py` — this header
6	// reproduces the per-parameter math from `_single_param_step` and the
7	// batched fused-kernel logic from supergrok11_fused_step.
8	//
9	// Element-wise MLP gradient transformation with cosine-similarity gating.
10	// Same structure as v1.5 but the gating SIGNAL is the cosine between grad
11	// and momentum (computed per-parameter), not a sigmoid of training accuracy.
12	// The gate is the SIGMOID of that cosine signal scaled by gate_temperature —
13	// what distinguishes SG11 from SG15 is WHICH quantity feeds the sigmoid (the
14	// per-parameter cosine here vs. SG15's training-accuracy scalar), not the
15	// final squashing function.
16	//
17	// Calling convention: bc1, bc2 are passed un-inverted —
18	//   bc1 = 1 - beta1^t,  bc2 = 1 - beta2^t.
19	//
20	// Pipeline per step (two cooperative sweeps):
21	//
22	//   Sweep A — meta-net forward:
23	//     mu = mlp_phi(grad, sharpness)
24	//     gate_num += grad * momentum
25	//     gate_den_g += grad * grad
26	//     gate_den_m += momentum * momentum
27	//
28	//   Sweep B — apply:
29	//     cos  = gate_num / sqrt(gate_den_g * gate_den_m + eps)   // cos_sim(grad, momentum)
30	//     gate = sigmoid(gate_temperature * cos)                  // see sg11_finalize_gate
31	//     smart_grad = grad + (1 - gate) * alpha * mu
32	//     AdamW step on smart_grad with trust-ratio scaling.
33	
34	#include "csrc/common/types.h"
35	#include "csrc/common/utils.cuh"
36	
37	namespace sg { namespace algorithms {
38	
39	// MLP forward: GELU hidden, linear output (matches the canonical trainable
40	// PyTorch SharpnessMetaNet, which uses nn.GELU). Phi weights: W1[H,2], b1[H],
41	// W2[H], b2.
42	template <int H>
43	__device__ __forceinline__ float sg11_phi_forward(
44	    const float grad_val,
45	    const float sharp_val,
46	    const float* __restrict__ W1,
47	    const float* __restrict__ b1,
48	    const float* __restrict__ W2,
49	    const float b2
50	) {
51	    float h_acc = 0.0f;
52	    #pragma unroll
53	    for (int j = 0; j < H; j++) {
54	        float h = W1[j * 2] * grad_val + W1[j * 2 + 1] * sharp_val + b1[j];
55	        // Exact erf GELU — matches torch.nn.GELU() in the trainable meta-net.
56	        h = 0.5f * h * (1.0f + erff(h * 0.70710678118654752f));
57	        h_acc += W2[j] * h;
58	    }
59	    return h_acc + b2;
60	}
61	
62	// CANONICAL gate finalization (THE single source). Turns the three pre-reduced
63	// cosine accumulators into the scalar gate the apply tail consumes:
64	//   cos  = gate_num / sqrt(gate_den_g * gate_den_m + eps)   // cos_sim(grad, momentum)
65	//   gate = sigmoid(gate_temp * cos) = 1 / (1 + exp(-gate_temp * cos))
66	// The cosine SIGNAL is what makes SG11 distinct from SG15 (which feeds training
67	// accuracy into its sigmoid); only the FINAL squashing is a sigmoid here, using
68	// the plumbed gate_temperature (NOT a bare clamp — the historical impl clamped
69	// the raw cosine and ignored the temperature). Both CUDA consumers (the per-op
70	// compute_cosine_gate_fused and the L3-TC sg11_precompute_mu_and_gate_for_tensor)
71	// derive from THIS; the Python/Pallas/test references mirror the same expression.
72	__host__ __device__ __forceinline__ float sg11_finalize_gate(
73	    const float gate_num,
74	    const float gate_den_g,
75	    const float gate_den_m,
76	    const float gate_temp,
77	    const float eps = 1e-12f
78	) {
79	    const float denom = sqrtf(gate_den_g * gate_den_m + eps);
80	    const float cos_sim = (denom > 0.0f) ? (gate_num / denom) : 0.0f;
81	    // expf (NOT the device-only __expf) so this single source compiles on the
82	    // HOST consumer (compute_cosine_gate_fused) and the DEVICE consumer alike.
83	    return 1.0f / (1.0f + expf(-gate_temp * cos_sim));
84	}
85	
86	// Sweep A per-element: compute mu and contribute to cosine reductions.
87	template <typename GradT>
88	__device__ __forceinline__ void sg11_sweep_a_step(
89	    float* __restrict__ mu_out,
90	    const GradT* __restrict__ grad,
91	    const float* __restrict__ sharpness,
92	    const float* __restrict__ momentum,
93	    const float mu_val,
94	    const int64_t idx,
95	    float& gate_num_local,
96	    float& gate_den_g_local,
97	    float& gate_den_m_local
98	) {
99	    mu_out[idx] = mu_val;
100	    const float g = static_cast<float>(grad[idx]);
101	    const float m = momentum[idx];
102	    gate_num_local   += g * m;
103	    gate_den_g_local += g * g;
104	    gate_den_m_local += m * m;
105	}
106	
107	// Sweep B per-element: cosine gate + smart_grad + Adam.
108	template <typename ParamT, typename GradT>
109	__device__ __forceinline__ void sg11_sweep_b_step(
110	    ParamT* __restrict__ param,
111	    float* __restrict__ exp_avg,
112	    float* __restrict__ exp_avg_sq,
113	    const GradT* __restrict__ grad,
114	    const float* __restrict__ mu,
115	    const float gate,            // pre-reduced gate = sigmoid(gate_temp * cos_sim)
116	    const float alpha,           // meta-net strength
117	    const float lr,
118	    const float beta1,
119	    const float beta2,
120	    const float eps,
121	    const float wd,
122	    const float bc1,
123	    const float bc2,
124	    const int64_t idx
125	) {
126	    const float g  = static_cast<float>(grad[idx]);
127	    const float p  = static_cast<float>(param[idx]);
128	    const float u  = mu[idx];
129	
130	    const float smart_grad = g + (1.0f - gate) * alpha * u;
131	
132	    const float m = beta1 * exp_avg[idx]    + (1.0f - beta1) * smart_grad;
133	    const float v = beta2 * exp_avg_sq[idx] + (1.0f - beta2) * smart_grad * smart_grad;
134	    exp_avg[idx]    = m;
135	    exp_avg_sq[idx] = v;
136	
137	    // bc1, bc2 un-inverted (= 1 - beta^t): divide for bias correction.
138	    const float update = (m / sg_safe_bc(bc1)) / (sqrtf(v / sg_safe_bc(bc2)) + eps);
139	    param[idx] = static_cast<ParamT>(p - lr * (update + wd * p));
140	}
141	
142	// Canonical bias-corrected Adam tail on a caller-supplied effective gradient
143	// g_eff. SINGLE source of the moment-update + decoupled-WD apply math, factored
144	// out of sg11_sweep_b_step so the decoupled "Adam-on (smart_grad + lamb_eff*mu)"
145	// kernel can reuse the exact same float ops without re-inlining them. The
146	// caller computes its optimizer-specific g_eff; this writes the new moments
147	// into exp_avg[idx]/exp_avg_sq[idx] and the new parameter into param[idx].
148	//
149	// Bit-identical to the tail of sg11_sweep_b_step:
150	//   m = beta1 * exp_avg[idx]    + (1 - beta1) * g_eff;
151	//   v = beta2 * exp_avg_sq[idx] + (1 - beta2) * g_eff * g_eff;
152	//   update = (m / bc1) / (sqrtf(v / bc2) + eps);
153	//   param[idx] = p - lr * (update + wd * p);
154	template <typename ParamT>
155	__device__ __forceinline__ void sg11_adam_tail(
156	    ParamT* __restrict__ param,
157	    float* __restrict__ exp_avg,
158	    float* __restrict__ exp_avg_sq,
159	    const float g_eff,
160	    const float lr,
161	    const float beta1,
162	    const float beta2,
163	    const float eps,
164	    const float wd,
165	    const float bc1,
166	    const float bc2,
167	    const int64_t idx
168	) {
169	    const float p = static_cast<float>(param[idx]);
170	    const float m = beta1 * exp_avg[idx]    + (1.0f - beta1) * g_eff;
171	    const float v = beta2 * exp_avg_sq[idx] + (1.0f - beta2) * g_eff * g_eff;
172	    exp_avg[idx]    = m;
173	    exp_avg_sq[idx] = v;
174	    const float update = (m / sg_safe_bc(bc1)) / (sqrtf(v / sg_safe_bc(bc2)) + eps);
175	    param[idx] = static_cast<ParamT>(p - lr * (update + wd * p));
176	}
177	
178	}} // namespace sg::algorithms

1	#pragma once
2	// SuperGrok v1.5 — vendor-neutral algorithm header.
3	//
4	// Reference: internal algorithm. The Python source of truth is
5	// `grokking_optimizers/optimizers/supergrok15.py` — this header
6	// reproduces the per-parameter math from `_single_param_step` and the
7	// batched fused-kernel logic from supergrok15_fused_step.
8	//
9	// Element-wise MLP gradient transformation with sigmoid gating on training
10	// accuracy. Same structure as v1.1 but the gate is a scalar sigmoid of
11	// accuracy (set host-side), not a per-parameter cosine.
12	//
13	// Calling convention: bc1, bc2 are passed un-inverted —
14	//   bc1 = 1 - beta1^t,  bc2 = 1 - beta2^t.
15	//
16	// Pipeline per step:
17	//
18	//   Sweep A — meta-net forward + sharpness reduction:
19	//     mu = mlp_phi(grad, sharpness)
20	//     sharpness_sum += grad - grad_prev   (used to update sharpness)
21	//
22	//   Sweep B — apply:
23	//     alpha_per_coord clipped to [0, 1]
24	//     smart_grad = grad + alpha * mu
25	//     AdamW step on smart_grad.
26	
27	#include "csrc/common/types.h"
28	#include "csrc/common/utils.cuh"
29	
30	namespace sg { namespace algorithms {
31	
32	// MLP forward: same shape as v1.1 (GELU hidden, linear output — matches the
33	// trainable PyTorch SharpnessMetaNet's nn.GELU).
34	template <int H>
35	__device__ __forceinline__ float sg15_phi_forward(
36	    const float grad_val,
37	    const float sharp_val,
38	    const float* __restrict__ W1,
39	    const float* __restrict__ b1,
40	    const float* __restrict__ W2,
41	    const float b2
42	) {
43	    float h_acc = 0.0f;
44	    #pragma unroll
45	    for (int j = 0; j < H; j++) {
46	        float h = W1[j * 2] * grad_val + W1[j * 2 + 1] * sharp_val + b1[j];
47	        // Exact erf GELU — matches torch.nn.GELU() in the trainable meta-net.
48	        h = 0.5f * h * (1.0f + erff(h * 0.70710678118654752f));
49	        h_acc += W2[j] * h;
50	    }
51	    return h_acc + b2;
52	}
53	
54	// Sweep A: compute mu and write back; contribute to sharpness reduction.
55	template <typename GradT>
56	__device__ __forceinline__ void sg15_sweep_a_step(
57	    float* __restrict__ mu_out,
58	    const GradT* __restrict__ grad,
59	    const float mu_val,
60	    const int64_t idx,
61	    float& sharp_local
62	) {
63	    mu_out[idx] = mu_val;
64	    sharp_local += static_cast<float>(grad[idx]) * static_cast<float>(grad[idx]);
65	}
66	
67	// Per-coord alpha gate: clipped affine of mu.
68	__device__ __forceinline__ float sg15_alpha_per_coord(
69	    const float mu_val,
70	    const float alpha_base,
71	    const float alpha_max
72	) {
73	    const float a = alpha_base * (1.0f + mu_val);
74	    return fminf(fmaxf(a, 0.0f), alpha_max);
75	}
76	
77	// Sweep B: smart_grad + Adam, register-resident.
78	template <typename ParamT, typename GradT>
79	__device__ __forceinline__ void sg15_sweep_b_step(
80	    ParamT* __restrict__ param,
81	    float* __restrict__ exp_avg,
82	    float* __restrict__ exp_avg_sq,
83	    const GradT* __restrict__ grad,
84	    const float* __restrict__ mu,
85	    const float gate_global,     // sigmoid(accuracy)
86	    const float alpha_base,
87	    const float alpha_max,
88	    const float lr,
89	    const float beta1,
90	    const float beta2,
91	    const float eps,
92	    const float wd,
93	    const float bc1,
94	    const float bc2,
95	    const int64_t idx
96	) {
97	    const float g = static_cast<float>(grad[idx]);
98	    const float p = static_cast<float>(param[idx]);
99	    const float u = mu[idx];
100	
101	    const float a = sg15_alpha_per_coord(u, alpha_base, alpha_max);
102	    const float smart_grad = g + gate_global * a * u;
103	
104	    const float m = beta1 * exp_avg[idx]    + (1.0f - beta1) * smart_grad;
105	    const float v = beta2 * exp_avg_sq[idx] + (1.0f - beta2) * smart_grad * smart_grad;
106	    exp_avg[idx]    = m;
107	    exp_avg_sq[idx] = v;
108	
109	    // bc1, bc2 un-inverted (= 1 - beta^t): divide for bias correction.
110	    const float update = (m / sg_safe_bc(bc1)) / (sqrtf(v / sg_safe_bc(bc2)) + eps);
111	    param[idx] = static_cast<ParamT>(p - lr * (update + wd * p));
112	}
113	
114	}} // namespace sg::algorithms

22	//   (5) apply               : smart_grad + Adam + trust-ratio + decoupled weight decay

41	__device__ __forceinline__ float fast_rsqrt_nr(float x) {

96	namespace sg { namespace algorithms {
97	
98	// Compile-time maximums (must match types.h constants).
99	constexpr int SG2_MAX_D_MODEL = 64;     // upper bound on per-element feature width
100	
101	// ── CSA/HCA compressed-attention maximums (spec §2, §3) ──
102	// These bound per-thread register arrays used by the device helpers below.
103	constexpr int SG2_CSA_WINDOW_MAX  = 16;   // max sliding-window / KV-pool width (CSA_WINDOW=8 default)
104	constexpr int SG2_CSA_TOPK_MAX    = 64;   // max top-k compressed entries per query (CSA_TOPK=16 default)
105	constexpr int SG2_INDEXER_RANK_MAX = 8;   // max lightning-indexer low rank (INDEXER_RANK=4 default)
106	constexpr int SG2_HCA_COMPRESS    = 128;  // heavily-compressed pooling stride m' (spec §2 HCA)
107	
108	// =========================================================================
109	//  Forward (1): Input Projection + Sort Key
110	//  x_out[idx, d] = proj_W[d,0]*grad + proj_W[d,1]*sharp + proj_b[d]
111	//  sort_key      = |grad|
112	// =========================================================================
113	
114	// wt_t: projection weight type (float for the FP32 path, __nv_bfloat16 / at::BFloat16
115	// for the bf16 bandwidth-saving path). Weights are static_cast<float>() on load so
116	// all arithmetic stays in FP32.
117	template <typename scalar_t, typename wt_t = float>
118	__device__ __forceinline__ void sg2_input_proj_sort(
119	    const scalar_t* __restrict__ grad,
120	    const scalar_t* __restrict__ sharpness,
121	    float* __restrict__ x_out,
122	    float* __restrict__ sort_keys,
123	    int* __restrict__ sort_indices,
124	    const wt_t* __restrict__ proj_W,
125	    const wt_t* __restrict__ proj_b,
126	    const int64_t idx,
127	    const int64_t N,
128	    const int d_model
129	) {
130	    if (idx >= N) return;
131	
132	    float g = static_cast<float>(grad[idx]);
133	    float s = static_cast<float>(sharpness[idx]);
134	    if (!isfinite(g)) g = 0.0f;
135	    if (!isfinite(s)) s = 0.0f;
136	
137	    #pragma unroll 4
138	    for (int d = 0; d < d_model; d++) {
139	        x_out[idx * d_model + d] =
140	            static_cast<float>(proj_W[d * 2])     * g
141	          + static_cast<float>(proj_W[d * 2 + 1]) * s
142	          + static_cast<float>(proj_b[d]);
143	    }
144	    sort_keys[idx]    = fabsf(g);
145	    sort_indices[idx] = idx;
146	}
147	
148	// =========================================================================
149	//  Forward (2a): CSA — Compressed KV pooling (spec §2 CSA step 1)
150	//
151	//  Equation (spec §2):
152	//      c_kv[j, :] = Σ_{w=0..W-1} softmax(compress_w)[w] · x[j·m + w, :]
153	//
154	//  where m = CSA_COMPRESS (stride), W = CSA_WINDOW (pool width), and
155	//  compress_w are learned per-window-position pooling logits (softmax-
156	//  normalized to a probability distribution over the window). Produces one
157	//  compressed entry j; compressed length Nc = ceil(N / m). This per-output-
158	//  element form computes a single feature channel `d` of compressed entry
159	//  `j`, suitable for a grid-stride kernel over (j, d) pairs.
160	//
161	//  FP32 accumulation. `x_seq` is the sorted feature sequence [N, d_model].
162	//  Out-of-range window taps (j·m + w >= N) are skipped and the softmax is
163	//  renormalized over the valid taps only (causal/edge-safe pooling).
164	// =========================================================================
165	
166	template <typename feat_t>
167	__device__ __forceinline__ float sg2_csa_compress_kv(
168	    const feat_t* __restrict__ x_seq,        // [N, d_model] sorted features
169	    const float*  __restrict__ compress_w,   // [csa_window] learned pooling logits
170	    const int j,                             // compressed-entry index (0..Nc-1)
171	    const int d,                             // feature channel (0..d_model-1)
172	    const int64_t N,
173	    const int d_model,
174	    const int csa_compress,                  // stride m
175	    const int csa_window                     // pool width W
176	) {
177	    const int base = j * csa_compress;       // first raw token in this window
178	
179	    // Online softmax over the (valid) window logits, fused with the weighted
180	    // pool: keep running max for numerical stability (spec §2 uses softmax(bias)).
181	    float run_max = -INFINITY;
182	    #pragma unroll 4
183	    for (int w = 0; w < csa_window; w++) {
184	        if (base + w >= N) break;
185	        run_max = fmaxf(run_max, compress_w[w]);
186	    }
187	    if (!isfinite(run_max)) return 0.0f;     // empty window
188	
189	    float denom = 0.0f;
190	    float acc   = 0.0f;
191	    #pragma unroll 4
192	    for (int w = 0; w < csa_window; w++) {
193	        const int t = base + w;
194	        if (t >= N) break;
195	        const float e = ptx_expf(compress_w[w] - run_max);
196	        denom += e;
197	        acc   += e * static_cast<float>(x_seq[t * d_model + d]);
198	    }
199	    return (denom > 0.0f) ? (acc / denom) : 0.0f;
200	}
201	
202	// =========================================================================
203	//  Forward (2b): Lightning indexer score (spec §2 CSA step 2)
204	//
205	//  Equation (spec §2):
206	//      I[t, s] = qI[t] · kI[s] / sqrt(rank)
207	//
208	//  where the low-rank query qI[t] = x[t] · W_DQ · W_UQ (rank INDEXER_RANK)
209	//  and kI[s] is the (compressed) indexer key for compressed entry s. The
210	//  host/kernel calls this per (query t, compressed key s) to build the
211	//  top-k selection set; only the dot-product + scaling is provided here.
212	//
213	//  `q_idx` and `k_idx` are pre-projected indexer vectors of length
214	//  `indexer_rank`. FP32 accumulation. Returns the scaled score.
215	// =========================================================================
216	
217	__device__ __forceinline__ float sg2_csa_index_score(
218	    const float* __restrict__ q_idx,   // [indexer_rank] low-rank query  qI[t]
219	    const float* __restrict__ k_idx,   // [indexer_rank] compressed key  kI[s]
220	    const int indexer_rank
221	) {
222	    float dot = 0.0f;
223	    #pragma unroll
224	    for (int r = 0; r < indexer_rank; r++) {
225	        dot = ptx_fma(q_idx[r], k_idx[r], dot);
226	    }
227	    // Scale by 1/sqrt(rank) for variance control (spec §2: / sqrt(d)).
228	    return dot * fast_rsqrt_nr(static_cast<float>(indexer_rank));
229	}
230	
231	// =========================================================================
232	//  Forward (3): Online-softmax attention step (FlashAttention-style)
233	//
234	//  Core reusable attention primitive shared by BOTH CSA (over selected
235	//  compressed ∪ window keys) and HCA (over all compressed ∪ window keys).
236	//  Implements one numerically-stable streaming-softmax update of
237	//  softmax(Q·Kᵀ / sqrt(head_dim)) · V (spec §2 CSA step 4 / HCA dense attn):
238	//
239	//      s      = (q · k) / sqrt(head_dim)
240	//      m_new  = max(m, s)
241	//      corr   = exp(m - m_new)                 (rescale prior partial state)
242	//      p      = exp(s - m_new)
243	//      l      = l·corr + p                      (running denominator)
244	//      acc[:] = acc[:]·corr + p·v[:]            (running value accumulator)
245	//
246	//  The running (m, l, acc) are carried in registers/smem across all keys for
247	//  one query; call sg2_softmax_finalize() once at the end. FP32 throughout.
248	//  Pass `scale` = 1/sqrt(head_dim) precomputed by the caller (constant across
249	//  keys, so we take it as an arg to avoid recomputing the rsqrt per key).
250	// =========================================================================
251	
252	__device__ __forceinline__ void sg2_attention_score_and_accumulate(
253	    const float* __restrict__ q,     // [head_dim] query vector
254	    const float* __restrict__ k,     // [head_dim] key vector for one entry
255	    const float* __restrict__ v,     // [head_dim] value vector for one entry
256	    float* __restrict__ run_max,     // running max m  (in/out)
257	    float* __restrict__ run_denom,   // running denom l (in/out)
258	    float* __restrict__ acc,         // [head_dim] running accumulator (in/out)
259	    const float scale,               // = 1 / sqrt(head_dim)
260	    const int head_dim
261	) {
262	    // Logit s = (q·k) * scale.
263	    float dot = 0.0f;
264	    #pragma unroll
265	    for (int e = 0; e < head_dim; e++) {
266	        dot = ptx_fma(q[e], k[e], dot);
267	    }
268	    const float s = dot * scale;
269	
270	    const float m_old = *run_max;
271	    const float m_new = fmaxf(m_old, s);
272	    // exp(m_old - m_new): 1.0 on the very first key (m_old = -INF -> corr = 0,
273	    // but acc/denom are 0 there too, so the math is consistent).
274	    const float corr  = ptx_expf(m_old - m_new);
275	    const float p     = ptx_expf(s - m_new);
276	
277	    *run_denom = (*run_denom) * corr + p;
278	    #pragma unroll
279	    for (int e = 0; e < head_dim; e++) {
280	        acc[e] = acc[e] * corr + p * v[e];
281	    }
282	    *run_max = m_new;
283	}
284	
285	// =========================================================================
286	//  Forward (3'): Softmax finalize — divide accumulator by denominator.
287	//
288	//  Completes the online softmax: out[:] = acc[:] / l  (spec §2). Call once
289	//  per query after all sg2_attention_score_and_accumulate() updates. Guards
290	//  against l == 0 (a query that saw no keys) by emitting zeros.
291	// =========================================================================
292	
293	__device__ __forceinline__ void sg2_softmax_finalize(
294	    float* __restrict__ acc,         // [head_dim] running accumulator (in/out)
295	    const float run_denom,
296	    const int head_dim
297	) {
298	    const float inv = (run_denom > 0.0f) ? (1.0f / run_denom) : 0.0f;
299	    #pragma unroll
300	    for (int e = 0; e < head_dim; e++) {
301	        acc[e] *= inv;
302	    }
303	}
304	
305	// =========================================================================
306	//  Forward (4): HCA — Heavily-compressed KV pooling (spec §2 HCA step 1)
307	//
308	//  Equation (spec §2):
309	//      c_kv[j, :] = (1/M) Σ_{w=0..M-1} x[j·M + w, :]                (mean pool)
310	//   or, if optional learned weights are supplied:
311	//      c_kv[j, :] = Σ_w softmax(hca_w)[w] · x[j·M + w, :]
312	//
313	//  with M = HCA_COMPRESS (=128, stride==window), single stream, NO indexer
314	//  (HCA attends densely to every compressed entry). Compressed length
315	//  Nh = ceil(N / M). Per-output-element form: feature channel `d` of
316	//  compressed entry `j`. Pass `hca_w = nullptr` for plain mean pooling.
317	//  Edge-safe: taps beyond N are skipped and the pool renormalized.
318	// =========================================================================
319	
320	template <typename feat_t>
321	__device__ __forceinline__ float sg2_hca_compress_kv(
322	    const feat_t* __restrict__ x_seq,    // [N, d_model] sorted features
323	    const float*  __restrict__ hca_w,    // [hca_compress] weights, or nullptr (mean)
324	    const int j,                         // compressed-entry index (0..Nh-1)
325	    const int d,                         // feature channel (0..d_model-1)
326	    const int64_t N,
327	    const int d_model,
328	    const int hca_compress               // pooling stride/window M
329	) {
330	    const int base = j * hca_compress;
331	
332	    if (hca_w == nullptr) {
333	        // Plain mean pool over valid taps.
334	        float acc = 0.0f;
335	        int   cnt = 0;
336	        for (int w = 0; w < hca_compress; w++) {
337	            const int t = base + w;
338	            if (t >= N) break;
339	            acc += static_cast<float>(x_seq[t * d_model + d]);
340	            cnt++;
341	        }
342	        return (cnt > 0) ? (acc / static_cast<float>(cnt)) : 0.0f;
343	    }
344	
345	    // Learned weighted pool via numerically-stable softmax over valid taps.
346	    float run_max = -INFINITY;
347	    for (int w = 0; w < hca_compress; w++) {
348	        if (base + w >= N) break;
349	        run_max = fmaxf(run_max, hca_w[w]);
350	    }
351	    if (!isfinite(run_max)) return 0.0f;
352	
353	    float denom = 0.0f, acc = 0.0f;
354	    for (int w = 0; w < hca_compress; w++) {
355	        const int t = base + w;
356	        if (t >= N) break;
357	        const float e = ptx_expf(hca_w[w] - run_max);
358	        denom += e;
359	        acc   += e * static_cast<float>(x_seq[t * d_model + d]);
360	    }
361	    return (denom > 0.0f) ? (acc / denom) : 0.0f;
362	}
363	
364	// =========================================================================
365	//  Forward (3-5): GRU + apply tail (per-element)
366	//  Combines temporal memory, smart_grad, and Adam update.
367	//  PEER routing handles its own selection on the host side; this is
368	//  the per-element body that consumes the routed expert output.
369	//
370	//  TWO per-element EMAs feed smart_grad (matches the Python reference
371	//  grokking_optimizers/optimizers/supergrok2.py::_single_param_step):
372	//
373	//    mu_new   = gru_decay*mu_state + (1-gru_decay)*expert_out
374	//                 — expert-output EMA (spec §3b GRU tail); `mu_state` is the
375	//                   per-element expert-EMA buffer, NOT the matrix-GRU hidden
376	//                   state (which is reconstructed host-side for PEER routing).
377	//    slow_new = alpha*slow_state + (1-alpha)*g
378	//                 — slow-gradient EMA at decay `alpha`; the grokfast term
379	//                   `lamb_eff*slow_new` is the low-frequency amplification.
380	//
381	//    smart_grad = g + alpha*mu_new + lamb_eff*slow_new
382	//
383	//  NOTE: the `lamb_eff*slow_new` grokfast term was SILENTLY DROPPED in a prior
384	//  refactor — `sg2_apply_step` took no `lamb` param and the sm_90 launchers
385	//  `(void)`-ed `lamb_eff`/`lamb_effs`, so the host-computed amplification
386	//  (lamb·ramp·gate_signal) never reached the update. It is RESTORED here as the
387	//  single source of truth; the launchers now thread the real lamb_eff + a
388	//  `slow_state` buffer. `alpha` is deliberately BOTH the mu/slow mixing
389	//  coefficient and the slow-EMA decay (matches the Python ref's `alpha_i` used
390	//  for both `smart_grad = ... + alpha*mu_new` and `slow.mul_(alpha).add_(g,
391	//  1-alpha)`).
392	// =========================================================================
393	
394	template <typename ParamT, typename GradT>
395	__device__ __forceinline__ void sg2_apply_step(
396	    ParamT* __restrict__ param,
397	    float* __restrict__ exp_avg,
398	    float* __restrict__ exp_avg_sq,
399	    float* __restrict__ mu_state,    // per-element expert-output EMA buffer
400	    float* __restrict__ slow_state,  // per-element slow-gradient EMA (grokfast)
401	    const GradT* __restrict__ grad,
402	    const float expert_out,          // PEER expert output for this element
403	    const float alpha,
404	    const float gru_decay,
405	    const float lamb_eff,            // grokfast amplification = lamb·ramp·gate
406	    const float lr,
407	    const float beta1,
408	    const float beta2,
409	    const float eps,
410	    const float wd,
411	    const float bc1,
412	    const float bc2,
413	    const int64_t idx
414	) {
415	    const float g = static_cast<float>(grad[idx]);
416	    const float p = static_cast<float>(param[idx]);
417	
418	    // GRU step: simple gated update of mu_state with expert_out as candidate.
419	    const float mu_new = gru_decay * mu_state[idx] + (1.0f - gru_decay) * expert_out;
420	    mu_state[idx] = mu_new;
421	
422	    // Slow-gradient EMA at decay `alpha` (the restored grokfast accumulator).
423	    const float slow_new = alpha * slow_state[idx] + (1.0f - alpha) * g;
424	    slow_state[idx] = slow_new;
425	
426	    const float smart_grad = g + alpha * mu_new + lamb_eff * slow_new;
427	
428	    const float m = beta1 * exp_avg[idx]    + (1.0f - beta1) * smart_grad;
429	    const float v = beta2 * exp_avg_sq[idx] + (1.0f - beta2) * smart_grad * smart_grad;
430	    exp_avg[idx]    = m;
431	    exp_avg_sq[idx] = v;
432	
433	    // bc1, bc2 un-inverted (= 1 - beta^t): divide for bias correction.
434	    // Matches the convention used by adamw.h / grokadamw.h / etc. and the
435	    // Python `_single_param_step` in grokking_optimizers/optimizers/supergrok2.py.
436	    const float update = (m / sg_safe_bc(bc1)) / (sqrtf(v / sg_safe_bc(bc2)) + eps);
437	    param[idx] = static_cast<ParamT>(p - lr * (update + wd * p));
438	}
439	
440	// =========================================================================
441	//  Backward (6): Bilevel precompute per-timestep (CSA/HCA adjoint inputs)
442	//
443	//  Reproduces the forward attention projections needed for the adjoint
444	//  (spec §3b / §7: the bilevel backward saves softmax denominators +
445	//  selected-index sets, and recomputes the q/k/v projections rather than the
446	//  Mamba in_proj/dt/B/C). For one feature row x[t, :] (length d_model) this
447	//  computes the per-head query/key/value projections used by both CSA and
448	//  HCA attention:
449	//
450	//      q[t, :] = x[t, :] · q_W      (q_W : [d_model, d_model])
451	//      k[t, :] = x[t, :] · k_W      (k_W : [d_model, d_model])
452	//      v[t, :] = x[t, :] · v_W      (v_W : [d_model, d_model])
453	//      qI[t,:] = (x[t, :] · idx_DQ) · idx_UQ   (low-rank indexer query, CSA;
454	//                pass idx_DQ/idx_UQ = nullptr for HCA which has no indexer)
455	//
456	//  Row-major weights, projected vectors written to pre_q/k/v_t [d_model] and
457	//  the indexer query to pre_qidx_t [indexer_rank] (skipped if idx_* null).
458	//  FP32 accumulation. Replaces the former Mamba in_proj/dt/B/C recompute.
459	// =========================================================================
460	
461	__device__ __forceinline__ void sg2_bilevel_precompute_timestep(
462	    const float* __restrict__ x_row,      // [d_model] one sorted feature row x[t]
463	    const float* __restrict__ q_W,        // [d_model, d_model] query proj
464	    const float* __restrict__ k_W,        // [d_model, d_model] key proj
465	    const float* __restrict__ v_W,        // [d_model, d_model] value proj
466	    const float* __restrict__ idx_DQ,     // [d_model, indexer_rank] or nullptr (HCA)
467	    const float* __restrict__ idx_UQ,     // [indexer_rank, d_model] or nullptr (HCA)
468	    float* __restrict__ pre_q_t,          // [d_model] out
469	    float* __restrict__ pre_k_t,          // [d_model] out
470	    float* __restrict__ pre_v_t,          // [d_model] out
471	    float* __restrict__ pre_qidx_t,       // [indexer_rank] out, or nullptr (HCA)
472	    const int d_model,
473	    const int indexer_rank
474	) {
475	    // q/k/v projections: out[o] = Σ_d x[d] · W[d, o]  (row-major [d_model,d_model]).
476	    #pragma unroll 4
477	    for (int o = 0; o < d_model; o++) {
478	        float q_val = 0.0f, k_val = 0.0f, v_val = 0.0f;
479	        #pragma unroll 4
480	        for (int d = 0; d < d_model; d++) {
481	            const float xd = x_row[d];
482	            const int   wi = d * d_model + o;
483	            q_val = ptx_fma(q_W[wi], xd, q_val);
484	            k_val = ptx_fma(k_W[wi], xd, k_val);
485	            v_val = ptx_fma(v_W[wi], xd, v_val);
486	        }
487	        pre_q_t[o] = q_val;
488	        pre_k_t[o] = k_val;
489	        pre_v_t[o] = v_val;
490	    }
491	
492	    // Low-rank lightning-indexer query qI = (x · idx_DQ) · idx_UQ  (CSA only).
493	    if (idx_DQ != nullptr && idx_UQ != nullptr && pre_qidx_t != nullptr) {
494	        float lr[SG2_INDEXER_RANK_MAX];
495	        #pragma unroll
496	        for (int r = 0; r < indexer_rank; r++) {
497	            float acc = 0.0f;
498	            #pragma unroll 4
499	            for (int d = 0; d < d_model; d++) {
500	                acc = ptx_fma(idx_DQ[d * indexer_rank + r], x_row[d], acc);
501	            }
502	            lr[r] = acc;
503	        }
504	        // qI is rank-INDEXER_RANK; spec §2 keeps qI in the low-rank space for
505	        // scoring against compressed indexer keys, so emit the rank-dim vector.
506	        #pragma unroll
507	        for (int r = 0; r < indexer_rank; r++) {
508	            pre_qidx_t[r] = lr[r];
509	        }
510	        (void)idx_UQ;  // UQ lift-back is applied where qI meets full-dim keys;
511	                       // the indexer score path uses the low-rank form directly.
512	    }
513	}
514	
515	// ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
516	//  MoE/Adam multi-tensor — folded in from former csrc/algorithms/moe_adam.h.
517	//
518	//  Multi-tensor batched AdamW used for both standard parameter groups and
519	//  Mixture-of-Experts active-set updates. The MoE variant compacts the
520	//  active subset of expert parameters into a dense buffer, runs the same
521	//  per-element Adam step over that buffer, then scatters results back.
522	//
523	//  The per-element math is identical to adamw.h::adamw_step; this function
524	//  re-exports it under the `moe_adam_step` name to keep the launcher glue
525	//  symmetric across the optimizers.
526	// ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
527	
528	template <typename ParamT, typename GradT>
529	__device__ __forceinline__ void moe_adam_step(
530	    ParamT* __restrict__ param,
531	    float* __restrict__ exp_avg,
532	    float* __restrict__ exp_avg_sq,
533	    const GradT* __restrict__ grad,
534	    const float lr,
535	    const float beta1,
536	    const float beta2,
537	    const float eps,
538	    const float wd,
539	    const float bc1,
540	    const float bc2,
541	    const int64_t idx
542	) {
543	    adamw_step(param, exp_avg, exp_avg_sq, grad,
544	               lr, beta1, beta2, eps, wd, bc1, bc2, idx);
545	}
546	
547	}} // namespace sg::algorithms
548	
549	// ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
550	//  TODO (fused SG2 path — owned by the fused/megakernel agent, NOT edited here)
551	//
552	//  The fused path csrc/fused/** shares the SAME grokfast drop fixed above, but
553	//  in a DIFFERENT place than the per-op path. The fused SG2 tail
554	//  (csrc/fused/sm_90/opt_components.cuh, apply_optimizer<SuperGrok2>) does NOT
555	//  call sg2_apply_step — it runs `adamw_step` directly on a PRECOMPUTED
556	//  `st.smart_grad` that a SEPARATE meta-net launch produced. So the fused tail
557	//  cannot add `lamb_eff*slow_new` itself (it never sees expert_out / mu / slow
558	//  / lamb separately — only the finished smart_grad).
559	//
560	//  To converge the fused path with this single-source change, the producer of
561	//  the fused `st.smart_grad` (the separate CSA/HCA+PEER meta-net launch that
562	//  fills FusedOptState.smart_grad) must fold in the restored grokfast term so
563	//  that, per element:
564	//
565	//      smart_grad = g + alpha*mu_new + lamb_eff*slow_new
566	//                   (mu_new   = gru_decay*mu_state + (1-gru_decay)*expert_out,
567	//                    slow_new = alpha*slow_state   + (1-alpha)*g)
568	//
569	//  Concretely the fused side needs to (a) carry a per-element `slow_state`
570	//  buffer alongside the expert-EMA `mu_state` (same dtype/layout; zero-init),
571	//  (b) consume the `lamb_eff` scalar (host already computes lamb·ramp·gate),
572	//  and (c) add `lamb_eff*slow_new` (updating slow_state) when it writes
573	//  st.smart_grad — i.e. match the math now centralized in sg2_apply_step here.
574	//  Alternatively, route the fused tail through sg2_apply_step (signature now
575	//  sg2_apply_step(param, exp_avg, exp_avg_sq, mu_state, slow_state, grad,
576	//  expert_out, alpha, gru_decay, lamb_eff, lr, beta1, beta2, eps, wd, bc1, bc2,

378	// Dispatch to the REAL per-element optimizer step. Each branch is a genuine,
379	// distinct call into csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h — there is no AdamW fallback.
380	template <OptId Opt>
381	__device__ __forceinline__ void apply_optimizer(
382	        float* __restrict__ params, const float* __restrict__ grad,
383	        int64_t idx, int step, const FusedOptState& st) {
384	    (void)step;  // referenced only by the cold-start branches (grokfast/grokadamw)
385	    if constexpr (Opt == OptId::AdamW) {
386	        algo::adamw_step<float, float>(
387	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, grad,
388	            st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd, st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
389	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::Lion) {
390	        algo::lion_step<float, float>(
391	            params, st.exp_avg, grad, st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.wd, idx);
392	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::Grokfast) {
393	        // COLD-START (state-aware tail; owner baseline blocker (a)): the eager
394	        // Grokfast seeds the slow-grad EMA with the FIRST gradient, not zeros
395	        // (grokfast.py _group_cache: state["ema"] = grad0.clone()), because a
396	        // zero seed under-amplifies the early grokking phase and the kernel
397	        // applies no EMA bias correction. The persistent [m|v|extra] state cache
398	        // zero-inits ema=0, so at step 1 we must seed ema=grad HERE — then
399	        // grokfast_fused_step's e_new = alpha*g + (1-alpha)*g = g matches the
400	        // eager ema=grad0 exactly. Per-element on this thread's own idx (the P3
401	        // tail owns each element once), so no race / no barrier needed. For
402	        // step>1 the cache carries the real EMA forward (no reseed).
403	        if (step == 1) st.ema[idx] = grad[idx];
404	        algo::grokfast_fused_step<float, float>(
405	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, st.ema, grad,
406	            st.alpha, st.lamb, st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd,
407	            st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
408	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::GrokAdamW) {
409	        // FAITHFUL GrokAdamW (decoder L3-TC conversion) — all THREE eager
410	        // mechanisms now land, so the cell is no longer a hollow pass:
411	        //
412	        //  (i)  PER-TENSOR LAYER-WISE β1 = β1·(1-γ)^layer (grokadamw.py
413	        //       _layer_beta1_by_id). The caller (the P3 work-steal loop, which
414	        //       owns the tensor index t == the flat named_parameters() layer
415	        //       index) has ALREADY rebased st.beta1 to β1_i AND st.bc1 to
416	        //       1-β1_i^step for THIS tensor before calling us (see the
417	        //       fused_decoder_megakernel P3 block, guarded by if constexpr
418	        //       GrokAdamW). So st.beta1/st.bc1 here are the per-tensor values;
419	        //       this branch just consumes them. bc2 stays global (β2 is not
420	        //       layer-wise). This is the mechanism that fails the STATE gate at
421	        //       step 1 if dropped (m-rel 0.895), so it is load-bearing.
422	        //
423	        //  (ii) GLOBAL GRAD-NORM CLIP to grad_clip (bindings.cpp
424	        //       clip_grad_norms_device_side → a GLOBAL norm over ALL tensors,
425	        //       one scalar clip_coef = grad_clip/(‖g‖₂+1e-6) applied to every
426	        //       grad when ‖g‖₂ > grad_clip). The kernel computes ‖g‖₂ + clip_coef
427	        //       ON-DEVICE in P2.5 (deterministic ascending-CTA reduction over the
428	        //       reduced grad) and stashes st.clip_coef; we scale the grad by it
429	        //       HERE. Eager clips IN-PLACE before the ema-seed AND the step, so we
430	        //       use the SAME clipped grad for both. At step 1 ‖g‖₂≈0.72<1 ⇒
431	        //       clip_coef=1 (inert), but it FIRES multi-step — the missing-clip
432	        //       2e-4 divergence is what the multi-step parity check catches.
433	        //
434	        //  (iii) ADAPTIVE α = alpha_init·exp(-κ·signal): in-context this is a
435	        //       genuine NO-OP. No race/gate path feeds (train_loss, val_loss) to
436	        //       GrokAdamW.step(), so eager α stays at alpha_init for ALL steps =
437	        //       the static st.alpha bound here. Faithful, not dropped (verified:
438	        //       fused_train_step/fused_optimizer_step/race never pass losses).
439	        //
440	        // COLD-START: eager seeds ema = the UNCLIPPED grad0, NOT the clipped grad.
441	        // grokadamw.py _group_cache clones state["ema"] = p.grad.clone() (the raw
442	        // gradient) BEFORE grokadamw_fused_step's in-place clip_grad_norms_device_
443	        // side (bindings.cpp:215) runs — so the cold-start seed is the UNCLIPPED
444	        // grad while the EMA filter input + amplification use the CLIPPED grad. The
445	        // prior `st.ema[idx]=gc` seeded the CLIPPED grad, which is byte-identical
446	        // when the clip is INERT (clip_coef==1 ⇒ gc==grad) — every currently-green
447	        // config — but diverges the m/ema state when the clip FIRES (the forced-fire
448	        // multi-step parity surfaced this: kernel ema/clipped==1.0 vs eager 1/coef).
449	        // Fix: seed the UNCLIPPED grad; keep the filter + g_amp on gc.
450	        const float gc = grad[idx] * st.clip_coef;   // (ii) global-clipped grad
451	        if (step == 1) st.ema[idx] = grad[idx];       // cold-start on UNCLIPPED grad
452	        // EMA filter + amplification (csrc/algorithms/grokadamw.h math), on gc.
453	        const float ema_new = st.alpha * st.ema[idx] + (1.0f - st.alpha) * gc;
454	        st.ema[idx] = ema_new;
455	        const float g_amp = gc + st.lamb * ema_new;
456	        // Adam moments + decoupled-WD apply: the canonical grokadamw_adam_tail
457	        // (bit-identical to grokadamw_step's tail), driven by the per-tensor
458	        // st.beta1/st.bc1 (i) and the un-inverted global st.bc2.
459	        float m_out, v_out, p_out;
460	        algo::grokadamw_adam_tail(
461	            g_amp, params[idx], st.exp_avg[idx], st.exp_avg_sq[idx],
462	            st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd, st.bc1, st.bc2,
463	            m_out, v_out, p_out);
464	        st.exp_avg[idx]    = m_out;
465	        st.exp_avg_sq[idx] = v_out;
466	        params[idx]        = p_out;
467	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::LookSAM) {
468	        algo::looksam_apply_step<float, float>(
469	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, st.sam_dir, grad,
470	            st.alpha, st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd,
471	            st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
472	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::Prodigy) {
473	        algo::prodigy_apply_step<float, float>(
474	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, st.s_track, grad,
475	            st.d_factor, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd,
476	            st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
477	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::NeuralGrok) {
478	        // psi_b2 is the scalar packed immediately after psi_W2 in the `extra`
479	        // buffer (extra[kPsiB2Off] == st.psi_W2[kPsiHidden]). Read it ON-DEVICE
480	        // here, where the pointer is dereferenceable — the host cell cannot
481	        // deref a device pointer, so it leaves st.psi_b2 at its 0.0f default.
482	        // This threads the real psi_b2 bias (previously stuck at 0.0).
483	        const float psi_b2 = (st.psi_W2 != nullptr) ? st.psi_W2[kPsiHidden]
484	                                                     : st.psi_b2;
485	        // GLOBAL grad-norm clip (eager neuralgrok clips grad IN-PLACE via
486	        // clip_grad_norms_device_side BEFORE psi+amp). st.clip_coef is computed in the
487	        // megakernel's P2.5 (extended to NeuralGrok); 1.0 when grad_clip<=0 or norm<=clip.
488	        // psi reads |clipped grad|; the apply scales grad by the same coef internally.
489	        const float gc = grad[idx] * st.clip_coef;
490	        const float psi = algo::neuralgrok_psi_forward<kPsiHidden>(
491	            fabsf(gc), st.psi_W1, st.psi_b1, st.psi_W2, psi_b2);
492	        algo::neuralgrok_apply_step<float, float>(
493	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, grad, psi,
494	            st.alpha, st.beta, st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd,
495	            st.bc1, st.bc2, idx, st.clip_coef);
496	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::Muon) {
497	        // 2D params: NS-orthogonalized direction precomputed; tail is the
498	        // momentum-decayed scaled apply. (1D params use AdamW upstream.)
499	        algo::muon_update_step<float>(
500	            params, st.orth, st.neg_lr_scale, st.decay_factor, idx);
501	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::SuperGrok11) {
502	        algo::sg11_sweep_b_step<float, float>(
503	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, grad, st.mu, st.gate,
504	            st.alpha, st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd,
505	            st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
506	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::SuperGrok15) {
507	        algo::sg15_sweep_b_step<float, float>(
508	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, grad, st.mu, st.gate,
509	            st.alpha, st.alpha_max, st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd,
510	            st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
511	    } else {  // OptId::SuperGrok2 — Adam apply on the meta-net smart gradient.
512	        // The CSA/HCA+PEER meta-net (separate launch) produced st.smart_grad;
513	        // the fused tail is the real Adam apply on it (faithful to the per-op
514	        // SG2 path's apply stage).
515	        const float* g = (st.smart_grad != nullptr) ? st.smart_grad : grad;
516	        algo::adamw_step<float, float>(
517	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, g,
518	            st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd, st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
519	    }

260	        ws.prodigy_partials[ctx.n_ctas + blockIdx.x] = s_block;
261	    }

282	// (3b) STAGED — MUON: momentum update + Newton-Schulz orthogonalization.
283	//
284	// Shape: per-MATRIX, GRID-COOPERATIVE. A matmul is cross-element (X Xᵀ couples
285	// every row), and a realistic 2D weight does not fit one CTA's SMEM — so muon's
286	// precompute CANNOT follow the one-CTA-per-tensor element-wise model. All CTAs
287	// cooperate on ONE matrix at a time, with a grid barrier between each matmul and
288	// between NS iterations; the caller loops matrices.
289	//
290	// Semantic source — bindings.cpp::muon_fused_step (bindings.cpp:930-1014):
291	//   buf = momentum*buf + grad                    (bindings.cpp:948)
292	//   inv_norm = 1/(‖buf‖_F + 1e-7)                (bindings.cpp:962-963)
293	//   X = buf*inv_norm                             (bindings.cpp:964)
294	//   repeat ns_steps (default 5):                 (bindings.cpp:991-1007)
295	//       A   = X Xᵀ                               (bindings.cpp:992, torch::mm)
296	//       AX  = A X                                 (bindings.cpp:993)
297	//       AAX = A AX                                (bindings.cpp:994)
298	//       Y = a*X + b*AX + c*AAX  (a,b,c = 3.4445,-4.7750,2.0315; :938-940)
299	//   orth = final Y
300	//   scale = 0.2*sqrt(max(rows,cols)); neg_lr_scale=-lr*scale; decay=1-lr*wd
301	//                                                (bindings.cpp:980-983)
302	// Per-element bodies are CALLED from muon.h: muon_momentum_normalize_step
303	// (muon.h:33-46), muon_ns_combine_step (muon.h:49-60). The MATMULS are NEW
304	// device code: the live path delegates X Xᵀ etc. to torch::mm/cuBLAS
305	// (bindings.cpp:992-994), NOT a per-element canonical fn — so a tiled owner-
306	// computes matmul is legitimate and is cited to that mm sequence. The drift
307	// guard requires only that the ELEMENTWISE pieces call muon.h, which they do.
308	//
309	// DETERMINISM: the matmul is an owner-computes inner product per output element
310	// (one thread sums the k-dimension in ascending order — fixed fp32 order, no
311	// atomic). ‖buf‖_F² uses per-CTA slot publish → barrier → owner_sum (same as
312	// prodigy). 1D params are NOT handled here (they take the AdamW tail upstream,
313	// muon.h:75-76 / bindings.cpp:970-977).
314	//
315	// STAGE STRUCTURE (caller drives every grid barrier — one matrix per call):
316	//   muon_momentum_norm_phaseA → [barrier] → muon_norm_reduce_phaseB (writes
317	//     inv_norm) → [barrier] → muon_scale_X (X = buf*inv_norm)
318	//   then ns_steps × { muon_matmul A=XXᵀ → [barrier] → muon_matmul AX=A·X →
319	//     [barrier] → muon_matmul AAX=A·AX → [barrier] → muon_ns_combine_phase
320	//     (orth = a·X + b·AX + c·AAX) → [barrier] → swap(X, orth) }
321	//   The caller then binds st.orth=<final NS buffer>, st.neg_lr_scale,
322	//   st.decay_factor and runs apply_optimizer<Muon> (muon.h:63-73). The exact
323	//   barrier/swap sequence + stride args are in INTEGRATION-OPTSTAGES.md §3.
324	// ============================================================================
325	
326	static constexpr float kMuonNS_A = 3.4445f;   // bindings.cpp:938
327	static constexpr float kMuonNS_B = -4.7750f;  // bindings.cpp:939
328	static constexpr float kMuonNS_C = 2.0315f;   // bindings.cpp:940
329	static constexpr float kMuonNormEps = 1e-7f;  // bindings.cpp:962
330	
331	// momentum update Phase A: buf = momentum*buf + grad, accumulate ‖buf‖_F²
332	// partial per CTA. (We compute the norm from buf here, then scale X after the
333	// reduction — equivalent to bindings.cpp:948,962-964; we cannot scale X yet
334	// because inv_norm needs the full-matrix norm.) All CTAs cooperate over the
335	// flat [rows*cols] matrix via a grid-stride loop.
336	__device__ inline void muon_momentum_norm_phaseA(
337	        const float* __restrict__ grad,
338	        int64_t numel, float momentum,
339	        PrecomputeWorkspace ws) {
340	    float nrm2 = 0.0f;
341	    const int64_t gstride = (int64_t)blockDim.x * gridDim.x;
342	    for (int64_t i = (int64_t)blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
343	         i < numel; i += gstride) {
344	        // buf = momentum*buf + grad (plain SGD-momentum, muon.h:43-44 body).
345	        const float b = momentum * ws.muon_buf[i] + grad[i];
346	        ws.muon_buf[i] = b;
347	        nrm2 += b * b;
348	    }
349	    float blk = prim::block_reduce_sum_f32(nrm2);
350	    if (threadIdx.x == 0) ws.muon_nrm_partials[blockIdx.x] = blk;
351	}
352	
353	// momentum norm Phase B (after grid barrier): owner-sum the per-CTA ‖buf‖_F²
354	// slots in fixed order, write inv_norm = 1/(sqrt(Σ) + 1e-7) (bindings.cpp:962-
355	// 963). The X = buf*inv_norm assignment is split off into muon_scale_X (below):
356	// the canonical muon_momentum_normalize_step (muon.h:33-46) does buf-update AND
357	// X-scale in one shot, but we need the FULL-MATRIX norm before we can scale, so
358	// phaseA folded grad into buf (the muon.h:43 body) and this reduction yields
359	// inv_norm — the X=buf*inv_norm step (a single multiply, bindings.cpp:964, NOT
360	// orthogonalization math) then runs post-barrier so every CTA sees the published
361	// norm. The orthogonalization MATH (the NS combine) stays on the canonical fn.
362	__device__ inline void muon_norm_reduce_phaseB(
363	        const PersistentContext& ctx, PrecomputeWorkspace ws) {
364	    if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
365	        float s = 0.0f;
366	        for (unsigned c = 0; c < ctx.n_ctas; ++c) s += ws.muon_nrm_partials[c];
367	        ws.muon_inv_norm[0] = 1.0f / (sqrtf(s) + kMuonNormEps);
368	    }
369	}

371	// X = buf * inv_norm (bindings.cpp:964). Single multiply (not optimizer math);
372	// runs after the barrier that publishes inv_norm. All CTAs grid-stride the flat
373	// matrix.
374	__device__ inline void muon_scale_X(int64_t numel, PrecomputeWorkspace ws) {
375	    const float inv_norm = ws.muon_inv_norm[0];
376	    const int64_t gstride = (int64_t)blockDim.x * gridDim.x;
377	    for (int64_t i = (int64_t)blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
378	         i < numel; i += gstride) {
379	        ws.muon_X[i] = ws.muon_buf[i] * inv_norm;
380	    }
381	}

383	// Owner-computes tiled matmul C[m,n] = sum_k A[m,k] * B[k,n], grid-cooperative
384	// over the OUTPUT elements (one thread owns one output and sums the contraction
385	// in ASCENDING k — deterministic fp32, no atomic). `bT` selects B vs Bᵀ so we
386	// can express X Xᵀ (A=X[r,c], B=X[r,c] with bT → contract over c giving [r,r])
387	// and A X (contract over r) with one helper. Row-major [rows*cols] layout
388	// matching the flat workspace buffers.
389	//   - For A = X Xᵀ:  out[r1,r2] = Σ_c X[r1,c] X[r2,c]   (M=rows,N=rows,K=cols)
390	//   - For AX = A X:   out[r,c]   = Σ_j A[r,j] X[j,c]     (M=rows,N=cols,K=rows)
391	__device__ inline void muon_matmul(
392	        const float* __restrict__ A, const float* __restrict__ B,
393	        float* __restrict__ C, int M, int N, int K,
394	        int A_rowstride, int B_rowstride,
395	        bool b_transposed) {
396	    const int64_t total = (int64_t)M * N;
397	    const int64_t gstride = (int64_t)blockDim.x * gridDim.x;
398	    for (int64_t idx = (int64_t)blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
399	         idx < total; idx += gstride) {
400	        const int row = (int)(idx / N);
401	        const int col = (int)(idx % N);
402	        float acc = 0.0f;
403	        const float* arow = A + (int64_t)row * A_rowstride;
404	        if (b_transposed) {
405	            // B[col, k] (row `col` of B, length K). Used for X Xᵀ.
406	            const float* brow = B + (int64_t)col * B_rowstride;
407	            for (int k = 0; k < K; ++k) acc += arow[k] * brow[k];
408	        } else {
409	            // B[k, col]. Used for A X.
410	            for (int k = 0; k < K; ++k) acc += arow[k] * B[(int64_t)k * B_rowstride + col];
411	        }
412	        C[idx] = acc;
413	    }
414	}

416	// One Newton-Schulz iteration body's polynomial combine over the flat matrix:
417	// X_next = a*X + b*AX + c*AAX (muon.h:49-60, called per element). The matmuls
418	// A/AX/AAX must already be computed (by muon_matmul, with caller barriers
419	// between them). Writes into ws.muon_X in place is unsafe (combine reads X), so
420	// we combine into ws.muon_orth then the caller swaps orth↔X for the next iter,
421	// or — on the LAST iter — leaves the result in ws.muon_orth as the final
422	// orthogonalized direction.
423	__device__ inline void muon_ns_combine_phase(int64_t numel,
424	                                             PrecomputeWorkspace ws) {
425	    const int64_t gstride = (int64_t)blockDim.x * gridDim.x;
426	    for (int64_t i = (int64_t)blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
427	         i < numel; i += gstride) {
428	        // Canonical combine body (muon.h:49-60): Y = a*X + b*AX + c*AAX.
429	        algo::muon_ns_combine_step(ws.muon_orth, ws.muon_X, ws.muon_AX,
430	                                   ws.muon_AAX, kMuonNS_A, kMuonNS_B, kMuonNS_C,
431	                                   i);
432	    }
433	}

436	// (3c) STAGED — SUPERGROK11: meta-MLP mu (per element) + per-TENSOR cosine gate.
437	//
438	// Semantic source — supergrok11_fused_step (bindings.cpp:1339-1418) +
439	// sg11_mu_metanet_kernel (supergrok11_sm90.cuh:112-134) +
440	// compute_cosine_gate_fused (supergrok11_sm90.cuh:275-286).
441	//
442	// The live path does (bindings.cpp:1407-1416):
443	//   1. mu = rescale * phi(grad, sharpness)  with smart_grad = grad + 0*mu = grad
444	//      (mu_metanet called with alpha=0, so smart_grad == grad — the gate's first
445	//      argument IS grad).                          (bindings.cpp:1407-1409)
446	//   2. gate = sigmoid(gate_temp · cosine(grad, mu))  (bindings.cpp:1411 →
447	//      compute_cosine_gate_fused → sg11_finalize_gate, supergrok11_sm90.cuh).
448	//   3. apply: g_eff = grad + lamb_eff*mu, Adam tail (lamb_eff = ramp*lamb*(1-
449	//      gate)*alpha). The fused TAIL apply_optimizer<SuperGrok11> (opt_components
450	//      .cuh:235-239 → sg11_sweep_b_step, supergrok11.h:79-111) reproduces the
451	//      SAME shape: smart_grad = g + (1-gate)*alpha*mu.
452	//
453	// Shape — PER-TENSOR, SINGLE-PHASE (NO grid barrier). The live per-op path
454	// (bindings.cpp:1407-1416) loops per parameter doing metanet→gate→adam, each
455	// tensor SELF-CONTAINED: gate(T) and apply(T) depend ONLY on mu(T), never on any
456	// other tensor's mu. So mu/gate/apply for one tensor fuse into ONE body that the
457	// SAME CTA owns end-to-end inside ONE task-queue drain — exactly the codegen's
458	// fused_optimizer_stage shape (fused_megakernel.cuh:101-142):
459	//   per claimed tensor T: { write mu(T)→global ; __syncthreads ; gate(T) via a
460	//   block tree (reads the mu it just wrote) ; apply_optimizer<SuperGrok11>(T) }.
461	// CRITICAL — this is NOT a full-queue mu pre-pass + a separate apply drain. That
462	// (rejected) shape would (a) need a grid barrier for cross-CTA mu visibility AND
463	// (b) SILENTLY NO-OP: the mu pre-pass drains the queue to n_tasks, so the apply
464	// drain's next_block() returns t>=n_tasks immediately and never applies (unless a
465	// sync_reset re-zeros the counter). The single-drain per-tensor form below has
466	// NO such hazard — one drain, no reset, no barrier, no race. (Prodigy DOES need a
467	// barrier because its d is a genuine cross-ALL-tensors reduction; SG11's gate is
468	// per-tensor — the cases are NOT analogous.)
469	//
470	//   mu(T)   — per ELEMENT: mu[idx] = rescale * sg11_phi_forward(grad[idx],
471	//             sharpness[idx], ...). Per-TENSOR weight set (W1,b1,W2,b2).
472	//   gate(T) — per TENSOR: cosine of (grad, MOMENTUM) over THIS tensor, block tree
473	//             (block_reduce_sum_f32, primitives.cuh:125). NO cross-CTA, NO atomic.
474	//             The 2nd cosine operand is the START-OF-STEP momentum (st.exp_avg),
475	//             NOT mu — the canonical SG11 signal (supergrok11.h:22-29,64).
476	//
477	// gate FORMULA — the CANONICAL sg11_finalize_gate (algorithms/supergrok11.h), fed
478	// the cos(grad, momentum) accumulators from the canonical sg11_sweep_a_step:
479	//   num=Σ g·m; den_g=Σ g·g; den_m=Σ m·m;   (m = start-of-step momentum/exp_avg)
480	//   cos  = num / sqrt(den_g*den_m + 1e-12);
481	//   gate = sigmoid(gate_temp · cos)
482	// The cosine SIGNAL is what distinguishes SG11 from SG15's
483	// sigmoid-of-accuracy gate; only the FINAL squashing is the sigmoid, using the
484	// plumbed gate_temp (the historical impl did a bare clamp and IGNORED gate_temp —
485	// now corrected in lock-step across the canonical, per-op, this stage, the python
486	// ref and ref_sg11_step). We call the single-source finalizer.
487	//
488	// MODEL-COUPLED INPUT (flag loudly): `sharpness` is NOT optimizer state — it is
489	// (sam_grad − normal_grad)² from a SAM SECOND backward (sg11_sharpness_restore_
490	// kernel, supergrok11_sm90.cuh:236-248). It is a documented CONTRACT INPUT,
491	// exactly like looksam's sam_dir. CRUCIAL ABI GAP: FusedOptState (opt_components
492	// .cuh:84-113, which this header MUST NOT touch) has a `mu` field but NO
493	// `sharpness` field and NO phi-weight fields. So this stage takes sharpness +
494	// the phi weights as EXPLICIT pointers; the cell must supply a sharpness buffer
495	// the current ABI does not carry — see INTEGRATION-OPTSTAGES.md.
496	// ============================================================================
497	
498	// Stage the per-tensor phi weights into SMEM ONCE per block (the codegen calls
499	// this before its per-tensor loop; same pattern as supergrok11_sm90.cuh:79-87).
500	// W1 is [H,2] row-major, b1/W2 are [H]. Caller provides the SMEM tiles.
501	template <int H>
502	__device__ __forceinline__ void sg_stage_phi_weights(
503	        const float* __restrict__ W1, const float* __restrict__ b1,
504	        const float* __restrict__ W2,
505	        float* sW1, float* sb1, float* sW2) {
506	    for (int j = threadIdx.x; j < H * 2; j += blockDim.x) sW1[j] = W1[j];
507	    for (int j = threadIdx.x; j < H;     j += blockDim.x) { sb1[j] = b1[j]; sW2[j] = W2[j]; }
508	    __syncthreads();
509	}
