511	// SG11 per-tensor body: write mu(T) to global AND compute the per-tensor
512	// gate(T) = sigmoid(gate_temp · cos(grad, MOMENTUM)) — the canonical SG11 gate
513	// SIGNAL (supergrok11.h:22-29, sg11_finalize_gate:64). The cosine's 2nd operand
514	// is the START-OF-STEP momentum (exp_avg) the caller passes in, NOT the mu just
515	// written: SG11's gate is cos_sim(grad, momentum), distinct from SG15's host
516	// accuracy scalar. mu is STILL written here (the apply tail's smart_grad reads it).
517	// Returns the gate on EVERY thread (broadcast through the reduction smem) so the
518	// caller binds st.gate before apply_optimizer<SuperGrok11>. The phi weights are
519	// already in SMEM (sW1/sb1/sW2 from sg_stage_phi_weights). `off`/`n` is the
520	// tensor slice; the SAME CTA owns mu(T) and gate(T) — no cross-CTA dependency, no
521	// grid barrier. gate_temp is the plumbed gate_temperature (FusedScalars.gate_temp).
522	template <int H>
523	__device__ inline float sg11_precompute_mu_and_gate_for_tensor(
524	        float* __restrict__ mu_blob,
525	        const float* __restrict__ grad,
526	        const float* __restrict__ sharpness,
527	        const float* __restrict__ momentum,
528	        const float* sW1, const float* sb1, const float* sW2,
529	        float b2, float rescale,
530	        int64_t off, int n, float gate_temp) {
531	    // Fused mu(T) write + gate(T) cosine accumulation, routed through the CANONICAL
532	    // sg11_sweep_a_step (algorithms/supergrok11.h:88-105 — the single source for
533	    // Sweep A): for each element it writes mu_out[gi]=rescale·phi(g,sharpness) and
534	    // accumulates the cos(grad, momentum) reductions
535	    //   num += g·m;  den_g += g·g;  den_m += m·m  (m = start-of-step exp_avg).
536	    // mu(T) = canonical meta-net forward (supergrok11.h:37-55) · rescale
537	    // (supergrok11_sm90.cuh:130). momentum is an INPUT indexed by gi (each thread
538	    // its OWN i=threadIdx.x stride indices), so no __syncthreads() is needed before
539	    // the reduction (the OLD form read the just-written mu_blob and DID need one;
540	    // reading the momentum input instead removes that dependency).
541	    float num = 0.0f, den_g = 0.0f, den_m = 0.0f;
542	    for (int i = threadIdx.x; i < n; i += blockDim.x) {
543	        const int64_t gi = off + i;
544	        const float g = grad[gi];
545	        const float s = sharpness[gi];
546	        const float mu_val = rescale * algo::sg11_phi_forward<H>(g, s, sW1, sb1, sW2, b2);
547	        algo::sg11_sweep_a_step<float>(
548	            mu_blob, grad, sharpness, momentum, mu_val, gi, num, den_g, den_m);
549	    }
550	    // Deterministic block reductions (fixed thread count). Three separate trees
551	    // (the live host fn does three independent .sum()s — same shape).
552	    num   = prim::block_reduce_sum_f32(num);
553	    __syncthreads();
554	    den_g = prim::block_reduce_sum_f32(den_g);
555	    __syncthreads();
556	    den_m = prim::block_reduce_sum_f32(den_m);
557	    // Canonical finalizer (sg11_finalize_gate, algorithms/supergrok11.h):
558	    //   cos = num / sqrt(den_g*den_m + 1e-12); gate = sigmoid(gate_temp · cos).
559	    // num/den_g/den_m are the cos(grad, MOMENTUM) accumulators from sg11_sweep_a_step
560	    // above — the same single source compute_cosine_gate_fused calls, no re-inlined math.
561	    return algo::sg11_finalize_gate(num, den_g, den_m, gate_temp);
562	}

567	// Semantic source — sg15_sweep_a_kernel (supergrok15_sm90.cuh:75-103) +
568	// supergrok15_fused_step (bindings.cpp:1512-...). mu[idx] = rescale*phi(grad,
569	// sharpness) — IDENTICAL shape to SG11's mu sub-stage (the phi-net shares the
570	// SG11/SG15 form, supergrok15.h:34-52). The DIFFERENCE from SG11:
571	//   * gate is GLOBAL = sigmoid(training accuracy), set HOST-side and passed as a
572	//     scalar (supergrok15.h:85 gate_global; threaded via FusedScalars.gate,
573	//     opt_components.cuh:153). So there is NO gate REDUCTION stage for SG15.
574	//   * the per-coord alpha clip (sg15_alpha_per_coord, supergrok15.h:68-75) and
575	//     smart_grad = g + gate_global*a*mu happen INSIDE the apply tail
576	//     (apply_optimizer<SuperGrok15> → sg15_sweep_b_step, opt_components.cuh:240-
577	//     244). So the ONLY precompute SG15 needs is mu.
578	//   * sg15_sweep_a also accumulates a sharpness² partial (supergrok15_sm90.cuh
579	//     :99-102, sg15_sweep_a_step → supergrok15.h:56-65). That sum updates the
580	//     NEXT step's `sharpness` input host-side; it is NOT consumed by THIS step's
581	//     apply (the apply reads mu + the host gate). It is therefore part of the
582	//     model-coupled sharpness pipeline, NOT this step's optimizer precompute, and
583	//     is documented in INTEGRATION-OPTSTAGES.md rather than computed here.
584	//
585	// MODEL-COUPLED INPUT: same `sharpness` ABI gap as SG11 (FusedOptState has no
586	// sharpness field) — flagged in INTEGRATION-OPTSTAGES.md.
587	// ============================================================================
588	
589	// SG15 per-tensor body: write mu(T) to global. NO gate stage (the gate is the
590	// host scalar FusedScalars.gate). Phi weights are already in SMEM (sW1/sb1/sW2
591	// from sg_stage_phi_weights). The codegen calls this inside its per-tensor loop,
592	// then runs apply_optimizer<SuperGrok15> over the SAME tensor with st.gate set to
593	// the host sigmoid(accuracy). Single-drain, per-tensor, no grid barrier.
594	template <int H>
595	__device__ inline void sg15_precompute_mu_for_tensor(
596	        float* __restrict__ mu_blob,
597	        const float* __restrict__ grad,
598	        const float* __restrict__ sharpness,
599	        const float* sW1, const float* sb1, const float* sW2,
600	        float b2, float rescale,
601	        int64_t off, int n) {
602	    for (int i = threadIdx.x; i < n; i += blockDim.x) {
603	        const int64_t gi = off + i;
604	        const float g = grad[gi];
605	        const float s = sharpness[gi];
606	        // Canonical SG15 meta-net forward (supergrok15.h:34-52), * rescale

614	//  optimizer_precompute_stage<Opt> — the uniform entry point the codegen calls.
615	//
616	//  STAGE SHAPES DIFFER per optimizer (do NOT force one pattern):
617	//   * Prodigy — a genuine cross-ALL-tensors reduction: this dispatcher runs
618	//     phaseA (drain queue, publish per-CTA (r,s) slots); the codegen then drives
619	//     a grid barrier (bar.sync_reset) and calls prodigy_precompute_reduce_phaseB.
620	//   * SG11 / SG15 — PER-TENSOR, single-drain, NO grid barrier. They do NOT run a
621	//     standalone queue drain here (that would silently no-op the subsequent apply
622	//     drain — see the SG11 block). Instead the codegen fuses mu(+gate)→apply per
623	//     tensor INSIDE its own task-queue loop, calling sg_stage_phi_weights once
624	//     per block, then per claimed tensor sg11_precompute_mu_and_gate_for_tensor /
625	//     sg15_precompute_mu_for_tensor, then apply_optimizer<>. This dispatcher
626	//     therefore does NOTHING for SG11/SG15 (the per-tensor helpers are the API).
627	//   * Muon — per-MATRIX, grid-cooperative: the codegen drives the explicit phase
628	//     fns (momentum_norm → barrier → norm_reduce → barrier → scale_X → ns_steps×
629	//     {matmul×3 + combine, barriers}) per matrix. Not foldable into this call.
630	//  See INTEGRATION-OPTSTAGES.md for each exact sequence.
631	//
632	//  A NOTHING-NEEDED / MODEL-COUPLED / SKIP optimizer must NOT be instantiated
633	//  here (static_assert guards it) — its tail already runs complete, or its input
634	//  comes from the model stage.
635	// ============================================================================
636	template <OptId Opt>
637	__device__ inline void optimizer_precompute_stage(
638	        const PersistentContext& ctx,
639	        float* __restrict__ params,
640	        const float* __restrict__ grad,
641	        const int* __restrict__ sizes, const int* __restrict__ offsets,
642	        const FusedOptState& st,
643	        PrecomputeWorkspace ws,
644	        // Optional model-coupled / meta inputs (param_init for prodigy).
645	        const float* __restrict__ param_init = nullptr) {
646	    static_assert(optimizer_needs_precompute<Opt>::value,
647	        "optimizer_precompute_stage instantiated for an optimizer that needs no "
648	        "precompute (grokfast/grokadamw/neuralgrok: math is in apply), is model-"
649	        "coupled (looksam: sam_dir from a 2nd backward), or is sibling-owned "
650	        "(supergrok2). See the verdict table at the top of this header.");
651	
652	    if constexpr (Opt == OptId::Prodigy) {
653	        // Phase A only (cross-ALL-tensors reduce). The codegen then grid-barriers
654	        // (bar.sync_reset) and calls prodigy_precompute_reduce_phaseB. param_init
655	        // is the trajectory anchor (flat blob parallel to params).
656	        prodigy_precompute_reduce_phaseA(ctx, params, param_init, grad,
657	                                         sizes, offsets, st.d_factor, ws);
658	    } else {
659	        // SG11 / SG15 / Muon are driven by their per-tensor / per-matrix helpers
660	        // inside the codegen's loop (SG11/SG15) or its per-matrix barrier sequence
661	        // (Muon), NOT by a queue drain here. This dispatcher intentionally does
662	        // nothing for them — see the helper fns above + INTEGRATION-OPTSTAGES.md.
663	        static_assert(Opt == OptId::SuperGrok11 || Opt == OptId::SuperGrok15 ||
664	                      Opt == OptId::Muon,
665	                      "unreachable: optimizer_needs_precompute gated the set");
666	        (void)params; (void)grad; (void)sizes; (void)offsets; (void)st; (void)ws;
667	    }
668	    (void)param_init;
669	}

3	// ============================================================================
4	// csrc/fused/sm_90/opt_stage_supergrok2.cuh — SuperGrok2's FULL CSA/HCA/PEER/GRU
5	// meta-net as IN-KERNEL STAGES of ONE persistent megakernel (Phase 3 of
6	// COMPONENT_CONTRACT.md: "SuperGrok2's CSA/HCA/PEER/GRU meta as in-kernel
7	// stages").
8	//
9	// WHAT THIS REPLACES
10	// ------------------
11	// The parity-validated per-op path (grokking_optimizers/kernels/sm_90/
12	// supergrok2_sm90.cuh :: csa_hca_step_one) runs the SG2 meta-net as ~15-20
13	// SEPARATE kernel launches PER PARAMETER TENSOR per optimizer step:
14	//   input_proj+sort | csa: project_q, compress_k, compress_v, win_k, win_v,
15	//   indexer_q, indexer_k, topk, attention, out_proj | hca: project_q,
16	//   compress_k, compress_v, win_k, win_v, attention, out_proj | matrix-GRU
17	//   (host ATen mm×3) | PEER routing+experts (host ATen) | sg2_apply.
18	// This header collapses ALL of that into ONE persistent kernel whose stages are
19	// separated only by in-kernel grid barriers — ZERO intermediate launches and
20	// ZERO HBM round-trips for the meta tensors (the whole meta weight bundle is
21	// 35.3 KB of fp32 with the defaults — dominated by the 144-expert codebook —
22	// and is staged ONCE into shared memory, re-read zero times across all stages
23	// and all parameter tensors).
24	//
25	// THE MATH IS UNCHANGED. Every device building block here is called VERBATIM
26	// from csrc/algorithms/supergrok2.h (sg2_input_proj_sort, sg2_csa_compress_kv,
27	// sg2_hca_compress_kv, sg2_csa_index_score, sg2_attention_score_and_accumulate,
28	// sg2_softmax_finalize, sg2_apply_step). The deliverable is LAUNCH-ELIMINATION,
29	// not a math change — the structure mirrors csa_hca_step_one stage-for-stage.
30	//
31	// THE SORT (honesty rail #5 — read this)
32	// --------------------------------------
33	// csa_hca_step_one sorts the per-tensor sequence by |grad| ASCENDING via a HOST
34	// torch::sort (grokking_optimizers/.../supergrok2_sm90.cuh:1642 `sort_keys.sort
35	// (0, descending=false)`). There is NO device sort kernel anywhere in the repo
36	// (verified). A global device sort would ALSO be wrong here: SG2 attention is
37	// per-tensor (each flat grad vector is its own length-N sequence; the
38	// task-queue processes many tensors), so a single sort over the packed param
39	// buffer would cross tensor boundaries. The sort is therefore left as ONE
40	// explicit pre-kernel step (a batched torch.argsort per tensor in the Python
41	// driver — see INTEGRATION-NOTES.md) producing `perm`/`unsort` index buffers
42	// the kernel consumes. Everything else is launch-free.
43	//
44	//   LAUNCH COUNT, per parameter tensor, per step:
45	//     before:  ~15-20 kernel launches  (+ host ATen mm/topk dispatches)
46	//     after:    1 argsort prep  +  1 persistent kernel   (whole batch of
47	//               tensors in the single persistent kernel via the task queue;
48	//               the argsort prep is ONE batched torch call for ALL tensors)
49	//
50	//   PATH TO ZERO EXTRA LAUNCHES: a device segmented-sort stage (bitonic over
51	//   each tensor's [N] keys, transcribed as barrier-separated passes) would fold
52	//   the sort in too. N here is tiny (a tensor's element count; the largest
53	//   race param is ~1e5) so an in-CTA bitonic per segment is feasible but is a
54	//   SEPARATE, larger piece of work; this pass does the honest maximal
55	//   elimination of everything else and flags the sort explicitly. The kernel
56	//   below is written so the sort stage can be dropped in as STAGE -1 (it only
57	//   needs `perm`/`unsort` populated before STAGE 0) with no other change.
58	//
59	// STAGE / BARRIER LAYOUT (per the decoder megakernel's discipline)
60	// ----------------------------------------------------------------
61	// gridDim.x = #SMs (one persistent CTA/SM), 256 thr/CTA. The whole step runs in
62	// ONE kernel. Because SG2 is PER-TENSOR (a tensor's attention couples only its
63	// own N rows), each CTA processes a DISJOINT set of WHOLE tensors pulled from
64	// the task queue and runs the ENTIRE per-tensor pipeline CTA-locally — so the
65	// only cross-CTA coupling is the task queue itself, and NO grid barrier is
66	// needed BETWEEN the meta stages (they are all within one CTA's tensor). The
67	// stages are sequenced by data dependence inside one CTA:
68	//
69	//   (per tensor t this CTA owns, looped over the task queue)
70	//   S0  input projection + |grad| key  (sg2_input_proj_sort, per element)   →
71	//       x_out[N,d], and gather x_sorted[N,d] = x_out[perm] using the
72	//       pre-computed `perm`.  [CTA-local, grid-stride over N]
73	//   S1  CSA context:
74	//        a. project q  = x_sorted @ q_W                                     →
75	//        b. compress c_k,c_v  (sg2_csa_compress_kv weighted pool + proj)    →
76	//        c. window  win_k,win_v = x_sorted @ {k_W,v_W}                      →
77	//        d. indexer qI = x_sorted@idx_DQ ; kI = pooled(x_sorted)@idx_K      →
78	//        e. top-k select (sg2_csa_index_score + insertion sort, per query)  →
79	//        f. attention (sg2_attention_score_and_accumulate over sel∪window)  →
80	//        g. out proj  csa_ctx = concat_heads @ out_W                         |
81	//   S2  HCA context (same shape; dense over all Nh + window, no indexer)     |
82	//   S3  matrix-GRU forward (z,r,h̃,h_new) per element, from
83	//        gru_input=[g,s,csa_ctx,hca_ctx]⊕h_old  → new_gru[N,gru_hidden];
84	//        write new_gru back to gru_state IN ORIGINAL order via `unsort`.     |
85	//   S4  PEER routing + experts (per head: query, product-key top-k of A & B,
86	//        k×k Cartesian, softmax(×10) weights, per-element expert MLP, head
87	//        average) → expert_out_sorted[N]; *= rescale.                       |
88	//   S5  unsort expert_out to original order, then sg2_apply_step per element
89	//        (smart_grad = g + alpha·mu_new + lamb_eff·slow_new, then Adam tail).
90	//
91	// Everything S0..S5 for one tensor is CTA-local; the per-tensor intermediates
92	// live in a caller-provided per-CTA workspace (sized for the largest tensor),
93	// re-used tensor to tensor. There is exactly ONE grid barrier in the kernel:
94	// after the whole task-queue drains, so the queue can be reset for a composing
95	// model stage if this tail is fused after a model bwd (see the launcher).
96	//
97	// DESIGN CHOICE — tensor-per-CTA (a CONSCIOUS divergence from design req #1)
98	// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
99	// Design req #1 asked for "CTAs partitioning the element/sequence space, ONE
100	// grid barrier between stages with cross-CTA dependencies (the sort and the
101	// attention windows are the couplings)" — i.e. ONE tensor at a time spread
102	// across the WHOLE grid, with a grid barrier after compress so all compressed
103	// K/V are ready before attention/topk. This header instead puts a WHOLE tensor
104	// on ONE CTA (the meta stages become __syncthreads-separated, no grid barrier
105	// between them), because SG2 attention couples only a tensor's OWN N rows — so
106	// the only genuine cross-CTA coupling is the task queue, and tensor-per-CTA is
107	// correct + far simpler + barrier-light.
108	//   THE COST (own it, don't hide it — honesty rails): with ~30 param tensors and
109	//   ~130 SMs, ONE 256-thread CTA does each tensor's entire CSA/HCA attention
110	//   (HCA is dense, ~N·Nh·heads·head_dim), and ~100 CTAs pull an empty queue and
111	//   idle at the final barrier. The per-LAUNCH path it replaces spread each
112	//   tensor's attention across the full grid, so this trades intra-tensor
113	//   parallelism for launch-elimination. That is a deliberate CORRECTNESS-FIRST
114	//   choice for this pass; the perf follow-up is exactly req #1's design —
115	//   sequence-space partitioning of the LARGE tensors with a grid barrier after
116	//   compress (the small tensors, which dominate the race's param count, are fine
117	//   on one CTA). The stages here are written so that refactor reuses the SAME
118	//   stage bodies (they already take explicit N/Nc/Nh and CTA-cooperative loops);
119	//   only the OUTER driver (who owns which rows) changes. See the report.
120	//
121	// DETERMINISM
122	// -----------
123	// No float atomics anywhere. Every reduction (projection dot products,
124	// attention online-softmax, expert MLP, GRU gates) is computed by a SINGLE
125	// owner thread for its output element in a FIXED accumulation order — the
126	// owner-computes pattern proven in the decoder cell (fused_decoder_megakernel
127	// .cuh P2) and F3's MoE-bwd. Each output element [row, channel] (or [row] for
128	// the experts/apply) is owned by one thread via a grid-stride loop; that thread
129	// does the full inner reduction itself. Across tensors there is no sharing — the
130	// result is deterministic (run-to-run identical) regardless of CTA scheduling.
131	//
132	// PARITY (NOT bit-identity) vs csa_hca_step_one
133	// ---------------------------------------------
134	// This matches csa_hca_step_one to fp32 round-off (the 1e-5 GPU parity target),
135	// NOT bit-for-bit. Two stages are the parity HOTSPOTS the gate should watch:
136	//   * matrix-GRU (S3) and PEER routing (S4): the reference computes these with
137	//     cuBLAS/ATen (torch::mm/matmul, torch::sigmoid/tanh/softmax). Here they are
138	//     hand-written sequential dot products + expf/tanhf. Accurate transcendentals
139	//     are used (expf, NOT ptx_expf) precisely so the only residual is FP
140	//     reduction ORDER (sequential vs cuBLAS tiling) — fp32 round-off, well within
141	//     1e-5. The CSA/HCA attention + compress stages, by contrast, DO use ptx_expf
142	//     because the reference kernels (sg2_attention_score_and_accumulate,
143	//     sg2_csa_compress_kv) use ptx_expf — matching them there is correct.
144	//   * PEER top-k uses descending insertion sort; the reference uses torch::topk.
145	//     Identical for distinct scores; tie-order is unspecified in both (low risk).
146	// The per-element apply (S5) calls sg2_apply_step verbatim — bit-identical there.
147	//
148	// PRECISION
149	// ---------
150	// fp32 compute throughout (matches the parity-validated apply and csa_hca_step_one
151	// — its detail:: helpers upcast bf16 weights to fp32 on load and accumulate in
152	// fp32). The meta weight bundle pointers are fp32 here (the Python driver upcasts
153	// the bundle once before the call; see INTEGRATION-NOTES.md). A bf16-COMPUTE
154	// follow-up would be a flag defaulting to THIS fp32 path, exactly like the
155	// decoder cell's bf16 TODO — see the report.
156	//
157	// PORTABILITY (COMPONENT_CONTRACT.md)
158	// -----------------------------------
159	// Self-contained: includes only the substrate (megakernel_common.cuh) + the
160	// algorithm header (csrc/algorithms/supergrok2.h) + CUDA. No globals, no repo
161	// build flags (the one tunable, SG_TUNED_MEGA_BLOCK, is #ifndef-defaulted). All state
162	// flows through the documented POD structs below + explicit pointers.
163	// ============================================================================
164	
165	#include "csrc/fused/megakernel_common.cuh"
166	#include "csrc/algorithms/supergrok2.h"
167	
168	#include <cuda_runtime.h>
169	#include <cstdint>
170	
171	namespace sg { namespace fused { namespace sm90 {
172	
173	namespace sg2alg = ::sg::algorithms;
174	
175	// ── Compile-time dims (defaults = supergrok2.py constructor + OPTIMIZER_CONFIGS).
176	//    Templated so a third project can instantiate other shapes; the race uses the
177	//    defaults. These bound the per-CTA shared/workspace footprint. ──────────────
178	template <
179	    int D_MODEL    = 8,    // input_proj out / attention model dim
180	    int NUM_HEADS  = 2,    // attention heads  (head_dim = D_MODEL/NUM_HEADS = 4)
181	    int GRU_HIDDEN = 4,    // MiniGRU hidden  (per-element carried state width)
182	    int NUM_EXPERTS = 144, // PEER expert codebook size (pk_dim = sqrt = 12)
183	    int EXPERT_HIDDEN = 16,// per-element expert MLP hidden width
184	    int NUM_PEER_HEADS = 4,// PEER routing heads (averaged)
185	    int PEER_TOPK  = 4,    // top-k per product-key axis (k×k experts/head)
186	    int CSA_COMPRESS = 4,  // CSA pooling stride m
187	    int CSA_WINDOW = 8,    // CSA pool width / sliding-window W
188	    int CSA_TOPK   = 16,   // CSA indexer top-k compressed entries
189	    int HCA_COMPRESS = 128,// HCA pooling stride m'
190	    int INDEXER_RANK = 4   // lightning-indexer low rank
191	>
192	struct SG2Dims {
193	    static constexpr int d_model      = D_MODEL;
194	    static constexpr int num_heads    = NUM_HEADS;
195	    static constexpr int head_dim     = D_MODEL / NUM_HEADS;
196	    static constexpr int gru_hidden   = GRU_HIDDEN;
197	    static constexpr int num_experts  = NUM_EXPERTS;
198	    static constexpr int expert_hidden = EXPERT_HIDDEN;
199	    static constexpr int num_peer_heads = NUM_PEER_HEADS;
200	    static constexpr int peer_topk    = PEER_TOPK;
201	    static constexpr int csa_compress = CSA_COMPRESS;
202	    static constexpr int csa_window   = CSA_WINDOW;
203	    static constexpr int csa_topk     = CSA_TOPK;
204	    static constexpr int hca_compress = HCA_COMPRESS;
205	    static constexpr int indexer_rank = INDEXER_RANK;
206	    static constexpr int pk_dim       = 12;  // sqrt(144); static for the default
207	    static constexpr int gru_in       = 2 + 2 * D_MODEL;          // [g,s,csa,hca]
208	    static constexpr int peer_in      = GRU_HIDDEN + 2 * D_MODEL + 2;
209	};
210	
211	// ── The SG2 meta weight bundle — fp32 pointers, staged ONCE into shared memory
212	//    at the top of the kernel and re-read zero times from HBM across all stages
213	//    and all tensors. Layout matches the per-op path's tensors (row-major). The
214	//    bundle, with the supergrok2.py defaults, is 9028 fp32 = 35.3 KB:
215	//      input_proj 8*2+8 = 24 ; csa q/k/v/out 4*64 = 256 ; compress_w 8 ;
216	//      idx_DQ/idx_K 2*(8*4) = 64 ; hca q/k/v/out 4*64 = 256 ;
217	//      gru Wz/Wr/Wh 3*(4*26) + b 3*4 = 324  (xin = gru_in+gru_hidden = 22+4 = 26);
218	//      peer Wq 4*(8*22) = 704 ; prod A/B 2*4*(12*4) = 384 ;
219	//      experts W1/b1/W2 3*(144*16) + b2 144 = 7056.
220	//    35.3 KB < the 48 KB static smem cap (and below the decoder cell's ~42 KB),
221	//    so dynamicSMemBytes=0 and the occupancy>=1 guard hold. The expert codebook
222	//    (7056 of 9028 floats) dominates — staging it in smem ONCE is the residency
223	//    win (every PEER lookup reads it, across all stages and all tensors). NOTE:
224	//    this 35.3 KB is the SMEM-resident copy; with the per-thread scratch (topk
225	//    16+16 ints/thread; peer/gru ~40-78 floats/thread) the kernel is smem- AND
226	//    register-heavy — occupancy is checked at launch (refuse if < 1 block/SM),
227	//    exactly the decoder cell's hang-freedom contract. ─────────────────────────
228	struct SG2Weights {
229	    // input projection (proj_W is [d_model, 2] row-major, proj_b [d_model])
230	    const float* input_proj_W;
231	    const float* input_proj_b;
232	    // CSA projections ([d_model,d_model] row-major) + pooling logits + indexer
233	    const float* csa_q_W;
234	    const float* csa_k_W;
235	    const float* csa_v_W;
236	    const float* csa_out_W;
237	    const float* csa_compress_w;   // [csa_window]
238	    const float* csa_idx_DQ;       // [d_model, indexer_rank]
239	    const float* csa_idx_K;        // [d_model, indexer_rank]
240	    // HCA projections ([d_model,d_model])
241	    const float* hca_q_W;
242	    const float* hca_k_W;
243	    const float* hca_v_W;
244	    const float* hca_out_W;
245	    // matrix-GRU weights (nn.Linear .weight [out=gru_hidden, in=gru_in+gru_hidden])
246	    const float* gru_Wz;  const float* gru_bz;
247	    const float* gru_Wr;  const float* gru_br;
248	    const float* gru_Wh;  const float* gru_bh;
249	    // PEER routing: stacked per head
250	    const float* peer_query_Ws;    // [num_peer_heads, d_model, peer_in]
251	    const float* prod_keys_A;      // [num_peer_heads, pk_dim, d_model/2]
252	    const float* prod_keys_B;      // [num_peer_heads, pk_dim, d_model/2]
253	    // per-element expert MLP (shared codebook, indexed)
254	    const float* expert_W1;        // [num_experts, expert_hidden]
255	    const float* expert_b1;        // [num_experts, expert_hidden]
256	    const float* expert_W2;        // [num_experts, expert_hidden]
257	    const float* expert_b2;        // [num_experts]
258	};
259	
260	// ── Per-tensor sequence-attention state ABI. The packed flat buffers carry ALL
261	//    parameter tensors back-to-back; tensor t occupies rows [row_off[t],
262	//    row_off[t]+n[t]). The per-CTA workspace is sized for the LARGEST tensor's
263	//    intermediates and re-used per tensor. The sort index buffers (perm/unsort)
264	//    are PRE-COMPUTED by the Python driver (the one explicit pre-kernel step).
265	struct SG2State {
266	    // Per-element optimizer state (packed across all tensors, element-indexed).
267	    float* exp_avg;        // [total]  Adam m
268	    float* exp_avg_sq;     // [total]  Adam v
269	    float* mu;             // [total]  expert-output EMA  (sg2_apply_step mu_state)
270	    float* slow;           // [total]  slow-gradient EMA  (grokfast)
271	    // Per-element matrix-GRU carried hidden state, ROW-major [total, gru_hidden].
272	    float* gru_state;      // [total * gru_hidden]
273	    // Pre-computed sort permutations, per tensor, ELEMENT-indexed into [0,n[t]).
274	    //   perm[row_off[t]+i]   = source row in ORIGINAL order for the i-th SORTED row
275	    //   unsort[row_off[t]+i] = sorted-row position of original row i
276	    const int* perm;       // [total]
277	    const int* unsort;     // [total]
278	    // Per-CTA scratch workspace (the meta intermediates, re-used per tensor).
279	    //   layout per CTA (floats), Nmax = max tensor numel:
280	    //     x_sorted   : Nmax * d_model
281	    //     csa_ctx    : Nmax * d_model
282	    //     hca_ctx    : Nmax * d_model
283	    //     q/c_k/c_v/win_k/win_v (csa): 5 * Nmax * d_model  (reused for hca)
284	    //     qI         : Nmax * indexer_rank
285	    //     kI         : ceil(Nmax/csa_compress) * indexer_rank
286	    //     sel        : Nmax * max(csa_topk,1)   (int, aliased in the float buf)
287	    //     concat     : Nmax * d_model
288	    //     new_gru    : Nmax * gru_hidden
289	    //     expert_out : Nmax
290	    //   The host computes the per-CTA stride (floats) and passes it as ws_stride.
291	    float* workspace;      // [n_ctas * ws_stride]
292	    int64_t ws_stride;     // floats per CTA
293	    int     n_tensors;     // == ctx.n_tasks
294	    const int*     n;          // [n_tensors] element counts
295	    const int64_t* row_off;    // [n_tensors] start element of each tensor
296	};
297	
298	// Per-tensor scalars that vary by layer (alpha/beta1/lamb_eff/bias-corr). Packed
299	// arrays the kernel indexes by task id. Shared scalars (lr/beta2/eps/wd/rescale)
300	// are in FusedScalars-style fields passed by value.
301	struct SG2Scalars {
302	    const float* alpha;     // [n_tensors] mu/slow mixing + slow-EMA decay
303	    const float* gru_decay; // [n_tensors] expert-EMA (mu) decay (== beta1_i)
304	    const float* lamb_eff;  // [n_tensors] grokfast amplification (lamb·ramp·gate)
305	    const float* beta1;     // [n_tensors] Adam beta1 (layer-scaled)
306	    const float* bc1;       // [n_tensors] 1-beta1^t
307	    const float* bc2;       // [n_tensors] 1-beta2^t
308	    float rescale;          // expert-output scale (shared)
309	    float beta2;            // shared
310	    float lr;               // shared
311	    float wd;               // shared (decoupled weight decay)
312	    float eps;              // shared
313	};
314	
315	// =====================================================================
316	//  Shared-memory weight bundle: a typed mirror of SG2Weights living in
317	//  smem. Staged once cooperatively by the whole CTA at kernel entry.
318	//  Sized at compile time from Dims. (~9 KB for defaults.)
319	// =====================================================================
320	template <typename Dims>
321	struct SG2SmemWeights {
322	    static constexpr int d = Dims::d_model;
323	    static constexpr int rk = Dims::indexer_rank;
324	    static constexpr int gh = Dims::gru_hidden;
325	    static constexpr int gi = Dims::gru_in;
326	    static constexpr int pin = Dims::peer_in;
327	    static constexpr int nph = Dims::num_peer_heads;
328	    static constexpr int pkd = Dims::pk_dim;
329	    static constexpr int ne = Dims::num_experts;
330	    static constexpr int eh = Dims::expert_hidden;
331	    static constexpr int half = Dims::d_model / 2;
332	
333	    float input_proj_W[d * 2];
334	    float input_proj_b[d];
335	    float csa_q_W[d * d];
336	    float csa_k_W[d * d];
337	    float csa_v_W[d * d];
338	    float csa_out_W[d * d];
339	    float csa_compress_w[Dims::csa_window];
340	    float csa_idx_DQ[d * rk];
